Official EU portal with recommendations by type of risk and citizen preparedness materials.
EU emergency service: rapid mapping of floods, fires and disasters.
112 works throughout the EU, free and from any mobile phone. Official guide on when to call and what to say.
Main source for the site: plans, recommendations and materials from the Ministry of the Interior.
The lists of what a prepared household should have: the basis of every kit here.
How mobile phone alerts (ES-Alert) work when there is an emergency in your area.
National coordination, Civil Protection and emergency response.
Healthcare provision, public health recommendations and crisis preparedness.
Food safety: preserving food without refrigeration and safe consumption during a crisis.
Official list of hospitals in Spain, with services and available beds.
Official health alerts and recommendations for the public.
Official forecast; this is where the alerts behind the heat, cold and DANA kits come from.
Warnings by hazard type and risk level: for planning before it arrives, not during.
Electricity system operator: information on the grid and supply.
Live demand curve. Useful for understanding a blackout or a consumption peak.
Water, energy and climate risks: the official framework for supplies.
Guardia Civil posts, emergency services and response in rural areas.
Police stations and emergency services in urban areas.
Volunteer support, evacuation and psychosocial care during and after an emergency.
Official publication of all the regulations cited on this site.
Floods, adverse weather events, wildfires and hazardous materials.
Base map for the /zona/ page (CC BY 4.0) and official geographic data for Spain.
Catalogue of open datasets from the Spanish public administration.
This is the source for the hospitals, pharmacies, police stations and shelters on the /zona/ map (ODbL).

Telecommunications and competition: information on coverage and communications services.

kit-suiza.titulo: Swiss Kit: the official 7-day reserve (9 litres of water per person)
kit-suiza.resumen: The list the Swiss government recommends keeping at home, translated and bought in Spain: 9 litres of water per person, food for a week, radio, camping stove, masks and cash. From 120 €.
kit-suiza.coste_total: 120-260 € per person for 7 days (less if you rotate what you already eat)
kit-suiza.paraQuien: For anyone who wants a household reserve with numbers, not good intentions: the official Swiss list translated for a Spanish apartment, with quantities, prices and what to rotate every six months.
kit-suiza.paraQuien_no: It is not an evacuation kit or a backpack kit: it is a reserve to stay at home. If your plan is to leave the city with just the clothes on your back, you need the evacuation kit. And it does not replace medication or the family plan.
kit-suiza.busc: emergency reserve kit 7 days water food camping stove

antes: Count water using the Swiss rule: 9 litres per person, and add for your pet and the heat in your area
Rotate the food: the reserve is normal food you eat and replace, not a separate cupboard that expires
Check the date on each water container and write it on the cap; bottled water expires too
Store chronic medication with its prescription in a cool place: it is the point no generic kit covers
Keep cash in small notes and separate from your everyday wallet
Test the camping stove and radio once a year, with new batteries
durante: Drink before you are thirsty: water is the first supply to fail and the hardest to improvise
Listen to the official radio twice a day; it is the channel that stays alive when the mobile network goes down
Cook during the day and with ventilation: a gas camping stove indoors kills with carbon monoxide if there is no air
Ration masks and disinfectant if you have to go out or clean contaminated areas
Do not open the fridge unnecessarily: each opening loses hours of cold
despues: Replace what you use within the same week, not 'someday': a half-finished reserve is not a reserve
Check dates and note what expired unused (it is usually what you do not like eating)
Clean the stove, dry the batteries and put everything back where you found it the first time

secciones.titulo: Water: 9 litres per person that do not depend on the tap
secciones.intro: It's the most specific figure on the entire Swiss list and the one most people fall short of without realising. Nine litres is a six-pack of 1.5 L bottles: drinking and cooking for a few days, not counting hygiene.

items.descripcion: The practical way to store 16 litres without taking over the kitchen. They stack, they rotate and they don't depend on the tap.

items.producto: Bottled water to rotate every 6 months
items.descripcion: A daily-use reserve that gets used up and replaced: that way the water never expires in the cupboard.
Turns questionable water into drinkable water. It's what separates 9 litres from a whole week when the supply comes back cloudy.

secciones.intro: Switzerland asks for a week of normal food: rice, pasta, oil, canned food, UHT milk, dried fruit, chocolate. No special rations; food you already eat, so you can rotate it.

items.descripcion: The base you can eat without cooking and without refrigeration. Alternate fish, pulses and vegetables so you're not always eating the same thing.
It keeps for years, fills you up and only needs water and heat. With the camping stove you cook it just like at home.
A pantry assortment to complete the week without depending on the fridge.
The detail that ruins a perfect pantry: without a can opener, cans don't open.

secciones.intro: Switzerland says it explicitly: a gas stove. Storing food and having nothing to heat it with is the most common mistake in household reserves.

items.descripcion: Hot coffee, rice and canned food with no power. With spare canisters and always used in a ventilated space.
If you have the space, a domestic heater gives you weeks of autonomy with one cylinder. Never inside a closed bedroom.
Lighters run out and won't light upside down. Long matches reach the burner without burning yourself.

secciones.intro: When the mobile network goes down, the radio keeps broadcasting. That's why it's on the Swiss list alongside spare batteries, and not the mobile phone.

items.descripcion: The information channel that survives a blackout. Tune in to the useful stations beforehand and write down the frequency.
Moving around the house without draining your phone battery, the one you need to make calls.
Hands-free for cooking, fixing things or going down to the garage. In a blackout, this makes the difference.

secciones.titulo: Hygiene and health: the 50 masks and medication
secciones.intro: The most surprising Swiss item: 50 masks per person. It was added after the pandemic because a health crisis also leaves people without supplies. At home, 20 FFP2 masks cover the domestic scenario.

items.descripcion: For going out, cleaning contaminated areas or living with a sick person without a healthcare system.
Cuts, burns from the camping stove and bumps are the real emergencies in a blackout, not movie-style disasters.
Rationed water means less cleaning: disinfectant makes up for it.

items.producto: Chronic medication: one week of your treatment
items.descripcion: The most personal item on the list and the only one you can't buy in a pack. With a prescription, in a cool place and with the expiry date in sight.

secciones.titulo: What Switzerland lists and almost nobody copies
secciones.intro: Cash, batteries and pet food. They are three lines from the Swiss leaflet that appear on almost no Spanish list and that in a real blackout you notice on day one.

items.descripcion: Keeps your phone alive for a full day and charges the radio if it is rechargeable. Charge it the same day you check your stock.
If you have a dog or cat, their week of food counts as much as yours. Almost nobody includes it.
When card readers and ATMs stop responding, cash still buys things. Sixty euros in 10 and 20 notes.

kit-basico-72h.resumen: EU resilience backpack: 21 verified items, tickable checklist, Amazon basket in 1 click. Updated 2026 guide.
kit-basico-72h.coste_total: 180-300 € (2-person household; first-aid kit and tools are per household, not per person)
kit-basico-72h.paraQuien: For any household in Spain, wherever you start. It is the resilience bag that the EU has called for since March 2025 — water, food, light, information, documents and warmth to last 72 hours without services — with every product checked: no listings that say one thing and sell another. If you are only going to put together one kit, make it this one.
kit-basico-72h.paraQuien_no: It is not a backpack for walking out, nor does it replace the specific kit for your risk (DANA, mountain, car). If you live in a flood-prone area or with people who need support, complete it with the evacuation kit and the baby kit or the elderly person kit.

antes: Prepare the kit with the whole family and keep it in a known and accessible place
Check expiry dates (water, food, batteries, medication) every 6 months
Write down emergency numbers on paper: 112, your municipal Civil Protection service

Activate mobile alerts in your phone settings: the ES-Alert system (National Alert Network) sends warnings directly to those in the affected area. The Basic Guidelines approved in April 2026 incorporate it into all civil protection plans
durante: Follow only instructions from official sources (112, Civil Protection)
Ration water and phone battery
Keep the battery-powered radio on and tuned to FM
despues: Replenish what has been used as soon as possible
Note down what was missing and adjust the kit

errores: Buying without checking the actual listing: half of the “essentials” lists online contain links to a women’s raincoat, a decorative poster instead of a map, or tablets for 200-litre tanks. Before paying, check that the photo, gender/size and dosage unit are the ones you need.
Buying only bottled water and having no plan B: if it runs out, a €10 pack of water purification tablets gives you treated tap or rainwater.
Storing everything in the storage room or the top cupboard. In a blackout, you have to find it in 30 seconds, better next to the door.
Not writing the purchase date on each pack: after two years you won’t know what is old and you’ll throw away half your stock.
Forgetting the radio. In a long crisis the mobile goes silent; the battery-powered radio is your only link with what Civil Protection instructs.
Buy everything in one go and leave it at that. It works better to add two or three items to each weekly shop.

secciones.intro: The first thing to run out and the only thing you can't improvise. 3 litres per person per day for drinking, a stored supply with a tap and a system to make questionable water safe to drink when it runs out.

items.producto: Bottled mineral water in 1.5 L bottles (6-pack = 9 L)
items.descripcion: Nine litres bottled: one person's 3 L/day for three days. Rotate every six months and use it for cooking.
Eight litres with a built-in tap: dispense without opening anything and it stands upright in the pantry. The household's base stock.

items.producto: Aquatabs water purification tablets (50 tablets, 1 L/tablet)
items.descripcion: One tablet per litre: 50 litres of drinking water per box. A clear dose for a bottle, not for a tank, which is what you really need.

secciones.intro: Food you can eat without cooking, without water and without electricity, and that you'll actually want to eat for three days straight.

items.descripcion: 515 kcal per serving, prepared with hot water in 8 minutes and eaten straight from the pouch. Shelf life of years.

items.producto: Sardines in olive oil (5 cans × 120 g)
items.descripcion: Protein and good fat with no fridge or cooking: open and eat. Five cans cover several lunches.
About 130 kcal per 35 g bar: a compact pocket snack, not a full meal. It adds to your supplies, it doesn't replace them.

secciones.intro: See and be seen, and keep your phone and radio alive. A headlamp keeps your hands free: it's the flashlight you actually use.

items.descripcion: 3 AAA batteries, 22 h on low and 6 h on high, red light so you don't blind anyone. Hands free for going down stairs in the dark.

items.producto: INIU 20,000 mAh power bank (22.5 W, USB-C)
items.descripcion: Four or five phone charges, with USB-C cable included. Your phone is your map, your flashlight and your radio: without battery there's nothing.

items.producto: AA and AAA alkaline batteries (24 + 24, 10-year shelf life)
items.descripcion: Twenty-four of each type, with ten years of shelf life. They power the radio, the headlamp and whatever comes next.

secciones.intro: Know what's happening and where the rest of the family is. With the network down, radio and paper win.

items.producto: FM/AM radio with hand crank, solar and USB (2,000 mAh)
items.descripcion: Three ways to charge it — hand crank, solar panel and USB — plus a flashlight and SOS button. If the internet and mobile network go down, it's the only channel still broadcasting.
The official map from the Ministry of Transport: roads, towns and alternative exits. It works without batteries and without signal.
Five whistles with cords: they can be heard much farther than a voice and use no power. The cheapest locator in the kit.

secciones.intro: Photocopies and some cash in small notes. Five minutes of preparation that save you months of paperwork.

items.descripcion: Waterproof closure: ID card, insurance policies, prescriptions and phone stay dry even if the backpack ends up in a puddle.
Two flat pockets worn under clothing: cash, cards and a copy of your keys kept close to your body. If you lose your backpack, you don't lose your documents.

secciones.intro: What keeps a small cut from becoming a problem in a place without running water or a pharmacy.

items.producto: Complete Lewis-Plast first aid kit (309 pieces, European standard)
items.descripcion: 309 pieces compliant with the European first aid kit standard: gauze, bandages, adhesive tape, scissors, gloves and dressings. A real foundation, not a decorative case.
1.5 litres of 70% gel: hand hygiene without water for days. One in the backpack, one in the car.
Fifty CE-certified FFP2 masks: smoke, dust and unhealthy air. The European list added them after the pandemic, and they still make sense.

secciones.intro: Keeping your body temperature up is what separates an uncomfortable night from a medical emergency. And wet = cold.

items.descripcion: Five large blankets that retain body heat and weigh 55 g each. One per person and two spare.
Unisex ripstop poncho, 8,000 mm water column, with hood and one size; it also works as a tarp. It covers the person and the backpack.

secciones.intro: Open, cut, screw and light. No battery, no signal and no relying on anyone.

items.descripcion: Blade, saw, can opener, corkscrew and screwdrivers in 60 grams. The tool that sorts out what you hadn't planned for.
Four boxes of XXL matches: they light a candle or a stove without burning your fingers and stand up to damp better than a lighter.

kit-dana.titulo: DANA / Flood kit: 14 items to protect your home (2026)
kit-dana.resumen: DANA kit: 14 items to protect your home from flooding. Guide based on official Civil Protection recommendations.
kit-dana.paraQuien: For anyone who lives or works in the Levante, the Balearic Islands, the Guadalquivir area, rambla (dry riverbed) zones, ravines or watercourses with housing nearby. DANA is the risk that recurs most often in Spain: water that arrives in minutes, with no adequate prior warning.
kit-dana.paraQuien_no: It isn't meant for the slow river flooding scenario in the north (there time is on your side and the priority is shutting off utilities and moving things out of the house). And it doesn't replace the basic kit: without drinking water and food, a DANA that cuts off roads drags on.

antes: Keep the basic 72h kit within reach
Don't leave loose objects on terraces or in gardens that could be swept away
If you live in a flood-prone area, prepare sandbags and get out of the basement
With an orange or red warning, keep alerts enabled on your phone: the new Basic Directive on flooding (BOE, 27/04/2026) consolidates ES-Alert as a direct channel for warning the public

Check the warnings before it rains, not once it's already coming down: at AEMET (aemet.es, Warnings section) or Meteoalarm, the European warning service. Civil Protection classifies torrential rain as above 60 mm/hour; with an orange or red warning, the day's plan changes: don't go out to run errands.

Move the kit, the documents and the charger up to a cupboard on the highest floor today. On the ground floor, in the basement or the garage they get soaked right when you need them, and the water won't let you go down. It's free and takes five minutes.
durante: Don't drive or walk through flooded areas: 15 cm of water can sweep a person away
Go up to the higher floors if water enters the house; don't use the elevator
Turn off the electricity if there is a risk of contact with water

If water reaches you in the car, leave it and go up to a tall building: a car floats and is swept away with less than half a metre of moving water. Never cross an underpass, a ford or a dry riverbed, whether by car or on foot: 15 cm of water is enough to knock a person off their feet.

Don't go down to the garage to move the car and don't go out to watch the flood: that's where serious accidents happen during a DANA. Stay on an upper floor with the radio on, and call or message anyone living alone nearby.
despues: Don't drink tap water until you've confirmed it's safe to drink
Don't turn on lights or devices until you've checked that the electrical installation is dry
Photograph the damage for insurance before removing anything

When cleaning up mud, wear an FFP2 mask, gloves and boots: dried mud is inhaled and comes from sewage. Open all windows and dry within the first 48 hours, or mold will stay in the walls and furniture.

Before drinking or cooking with tap water, check with your local council that the supply is safe: after a flood there may be a boil-water notice. If in any doubt, use bottled water or boil it for one minute.

errores: Relying on the mobile alert and having nothing ready until it sounds. In the 2024 DANA, many people had no time: the kit must be prepared beforehand.
Going down to the garage or storage room to save things when it's already raining hard. That's the typical accident.
Turning on the light or touching wet sockets: electrocution on the ground floor is one of the most common causes of death in floods.
Returning too early and walking through mud without gloves or boots: it's full of sewage, glass and metal.

Not noting or photographing anything: damage claims are poorly declared without evidence and the deadlines of the Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros run. Take dated photos and video from the first day, including of what you throw away. And don't store the kit in the basement: the place that floods first is the worst for emergency supplies.

secciones.intro: If you're caught on foot or driving, what you decide in two minutes matters more than everything you buy afterwards.

items.descripcion: Fitted hood and sealed seams for torrential rain.
Knee-high rubber boots: contaminated water, mud and sharp objects.
Protection when handling debris and working in water.

secciones.intro: In a flooded home, the biggest silent risk is not the water: it is the electricity still in the wiring.

items.descripcion: LED model with 100+ lumens. Carry spare batteries separately.
Protection against electrocution when reconnecting power in wet areas.

secciones.intro: Cheap, quick measures to put in place when there is a warning, before the water arrives.

items.descripcion: Improvised water barriers at low doors and windows.

items.producto: Tape and plastic sheeting to seal windows
items.descripcion: Sealing windows and cracks ahead of wind-driven rain.

secciones.intro: The days after are when injuries and illness happen: mud, damp and damaged installations.

items.descripcion: DANA floodwater leaves mud mixed with sewage: disinfect everything.

items.producto: Wide shovel for clearing mud or snow
items.descripcion: Remove mud and standing water after the floodwater has passed.
Prevents mold and structural damp after flooding.

secciones.titulo: Communication and alerts: when the network goes down
secciones.intro: In a DANA, coverage is the first thing to fail: if your mobile loses signal and there is no power, this is what alerts you and keeps you connected. Everything works without coverage or installation.

items.producto: Battery-powered or hand-crank FM/AM radio with built-in flashlight
items.descripcion: Mobile networks and power go out just when information is needed most. Buy a radio with a large dial, write the regional station and Radio Nacional on the lid, and test it once a month: official alerts are still broadcast on radio and through municipal loudspeakers. Keep spare batteries separately, outside the device.

With the mobile network down, two people 300–500 m apart in a flooded village can still talk: PMR446 radios are legal in Spain without a license, with common-use channels. They are useful so one person can queue at the distribution point while the other stays with someone who cannot move. How to use them, in the PMR446 guide on the blog.

items.producto: External battery (power bank) 10,000–20,000 mAh, two outputs
items.descripcion: Without power, your phone is your flashlight, your map and your link to family: it runs out in hours. Charge it to 100 % when the orange warning comes and don't burn it on videos; a small solar panel or the car charger tops it up again. Keep the short cable in the same bag.

items.producto: FFP2 mask (pack) and protective goggles for clean-up
items.descripcion: Flood mud carries sewage and, when it dries, you breathe it in: when clearing mud and knocking down wet walls, mask on and eyes covered. Use it from day one, not when it already smells. If you have asthma or breathing problems, do it with someone else present and take breaks.

kit-apagon.titulo: Blackout Kit: 15 items to survive without power (2026)
kit-apagon.resumen: Blackout Kit: 15 items to survive without electricity. Guide based on the EU Preparedness Strategy (2025).
kit-apagon.coste_total: 90-200 € for the essentials; 257-525 € with all the recommended items (SAI, solar panel, fire extinguisher...) — on top of the basic kit
kit-apagon.paraQuien: For everyone. On 28 April 2025 the peninsula went 12 hours or more without power: dead traffic lights, closed ATMs, stopped elevators, supermarkets with no card terminals. A long blackout is not an anecdote: it's a day without being able to buy, without water on upper floors and without an elevator.
kit-apagon.paraQuien_no: It won't help if what you expect is to keep working or studying as normal: that needs power generation capacity (a large panel, a home battery), which is another level of investment. And if you live on the fifth floor with no elevator, remember that the water you go down to fetch has to be carried back up on foot.

antes: Charge phones and power banks daily if there's a warning of grid strain
Keep cash at home: card terminals don't work without power
A gas canister or camping stove to eat something hot
Leave two frozen water bottles or gel packs in the freezer: on the day of the outage they move to the fridge and give you hours of cold without opening the door.
Test the CO detector today with its test button and check that the extinguisher gauge is in the green. In a blackout there's no time to discover they don't work.
durante: Don't use candles as your main light: always a flashlight
Unplug sensitive appliances to avoid surges when the power comes back
Save phone battery: calls and SMS only (the data network may go down)

No combustion appliances in a closed room: no braziers, barbecues, generators or gas stoves inside the house or garage. If you light the stove, use cross-ventilation (one window and another opening) and keep a CO detector in view.
Organise the fridge by thawing: milk, meat, fish and cold cuts first; frozen and canned goods last. Anything already thawed must be cooked or thrown away: do not refreeze it.
With SAI, turn off the computer and leave only the router: you keep Wi-Fi while the battery lasts and avoid the voltage spike when the power returns.
despues: Recharge everything again and restock what you used
Check food that has lost the cold chain
Before going to sleep, ventilate the room where you used a flame and check the CO detector and fire extinguisher again.
Restock what you used: batteries, candles, freezer gel and anything you opened from the pantry. The next outage won't warn you.

errores: Opening the fridge every so often to see what's inside. Kept closed and unopened, a fridge lasts about 4 hours and a full freezer up to 24-48 hours.
Lighting candles and leaving them unattended: it is the classic cause of house fires during power cuts. With children, a flashlight and that's it.
Not unplugging appliances: when the power comes back, the surge can fry the fridge, the boiler or the router.
Relying on your phone having battery: during outages people call at the same time and the antennas don't hold up for long. Airplane mode and a full power bank.
Paying by card and discovering the card terminal doesn't work. Cash in small notes is the plan, not a minor detail.

secciones.intro: One light per person, and not candles. Magnetic lamps hang inside the fridge or cupboard and make a huge difference.

items.producto: Rechargeable LED lamps with a magnet (for fridge/pantry)
items.descripcion: It sticks to the fridge, pantry or car hood. Hands-free.
It provides light hands-free: essential for working at night.

items.producto: Emergency candles (backup only, with a safe candle holder)
items.descripcion: Backup lighting, never the main source. With a metal candle holder.

secciones.intro: Keep your phone and radio alive for 3-4 days. A large power bank, a small panel to recharge it and a dynamo charger as a last resort.

items.producto: Power bank ≥ 20,000 mAh with AC output or USB-C PD
items.descripcion: 20,000 mAh power bank: 4-5 full phone charges.
Recharge the power bank with solar. 20-40 W charges a phone in 3-4 hours.
Hand crank: infinite power without sun or grid.

secciones.intro: Being able to make a coffee or heat water makes a real difference to morale during a blackout. And you must do it in a ventilated area: butane in an enclosed room kills.

items.descripcion: Hot food without electricity. Always use in a ventilated area.
Protein and calories without refrigeration. Prioritize legumes and fish.

items.producto: Freezer blocks (freezable gel packs) for fridge and freezer
items.descripcion: Keep them frozen beforehand: on the day of the outage, move them to the fridge, next to the most delicate items (meat, fish, dairy, cold cuts), and they extend the cold hours without you having to open the door to check anything. Equivalent free trick: two frozen water bottles. And anything that has already thawed must not be refrozen: cook it or throw it away.

secciones.intro: A blackout changes how you cook and how you light your home, and that brings two invisible risks: carbon monoxide and fire. They are two small purchases that are almost never used and that, on the day they are needed, are the only ones that matter.

items.producto: Battery-powered carbon monoxide (CO) detector with alarm
items.descripcion: CO has no smell, is invisible and does not irritate: it makes you sleepy, gives you a headache and, if you stay in the room, kills you in your sleep. During a blackout people light candles, stoves and braziers, and that is where it appears. Put it at head height, outside the bathroom and near the area where you cook, and press the test button every time the clocks change. Non-negotiable rule: braziers, barbecues, generators and stoves never in a closed room or in the garage.

secciones.intro: Cash, paper contacts and a radio. When everything is digital, analog decides.

items.descripcion: Store cash and critical documents at home.

items.producto: FM/AM radio with hand crank and solar panel
items.descripcion: Only source of information if internet and phone networks go down. Built-in battery, hand crank and solar: no need for disposable batteries.

items.producto: Small SAI / UPS (600-900 VA) for router and ONT
items.descripcion: A 600-900 VA UPS keeps the router and the ONT running for as long as its battery lasts (usually minutes, not hours) and, as a bonus, protects the equipment from power surges when the power comes back on. Connect only the router: if you also plug the computer or the TV into it, the battery runs out almost immediately. It is not a generator: it won't power a fridge, heating or a washing machine.

kit-coche.titulo: Car Kit 2026: DGT mandatory and optional items
kit-coche.resumen: DGT mandatory car kit 2026: V-16 beacon, vest and all the essentials. Verified list and Amazon basket in 1 click.
kit-coche.coste_total: €60-120 (not counting the V-16 beacon, which is mandatory)
kit-coche.paraQuien: For anyone who drives, which is almost all of us. Beyond what the law requires, it is what you need if you break down on a mountain pass in January, in a 6-hour traffic jam in August or waiting for a tow truck at 3 in the morning.
kit-coche.paraQuien_no: It is not a workshop kit: if you expect to change a wheel yourself or charge a battery, you also need a jack, a wheel brace and jump leads, and to know how to use them. And it does not replace the backpack you carry with you: the car may end up somewhere you don't want to be.

antes: Check tyres, battery and fluid levels before long journeys
Check the condition of the kit at every change of season
durante: If you break down, signal from inside the car with the approved connected V-16 beacon: it is the only legal method since 1/1/2026 (RD 159/2021; DGT, note of 25/11/2025). Warning triangles are no longer valid
Don't get out of the car in snow if there is traffic: inside is safer and warmer

From 1/10/2026, when passing a vehicle stopped by a breakdown or accident, reduce the road's speed limit by at least 20 km/h and leave 1.5 m of lateral clearance; in traffic jams, open the central emergency lane for ambulances and tow trucks (RD 518/2026 of 24 June, BOE-A-2026-13889, published 26/06/2026)

From 1/10/2026, seat belts are always mandatory: the reform of the General Traffic Regulations removes the exemptions for taxi drivers, delivery drivers and driving school instructors; only patients in an ambulance on an emergency call are exempt (RD 518/2026, art. 119.2, BOE-A-2026-13889)

From 1/10/2026, on motorways and dual carriageways where the road is made difficult by snow, overtaking is prohibited and you must drive in the right-hand lane (the adjacent lane if there are three or more), leaving the left-hand lanes free for snowplows and emergencies (RD 518/2026, Article 32 of the General Traffic Regulations, BOE-A-2026-13889)
despues: Replace what you have used (batteries, water, fuel) when you get home

errores: Not checking the V-16 beacon: the connection expires (it usually lasts about 12 years from manufacture) and there are models without DGT approval. Using triangles is no longer valid from 1/1/2026.
Having the kit in the trunk and the trunk full of things from the last move. A first-aid kit that is covered up does not exist.
Not checking the spare tire or the water level: a puncture 30 km from the nearest gas station is an hours-long problem.
Relying on your phone with 8% battery and no power bank in the car.
In snow, setting off without chains or not knowing how to fit them. Textile snow socks are a legal workaround in some places and a danger in others: learn beforehand what your area allows.

secciones.intro: What they can require of you during an inspection or at an accident. Since 1/1/2026 the connected V-16 beacon is the only legal means of signaling.

items.descripcion: From 1 January 2026 they are no longer valid for signaling in Spain (replaced by the connected V-16 beacon); still useful for travel to countries outside the Vienna Convention.

items.producto: Approved connected V-16 beacon (only legal means since 1/1/2026)
items.descripcion: Mandatory since 1 January 2026: it replaces triangles. Only approved models connected to the DGT are valid (official list at dgt.es). Check the IDIADA/LCOE certificate engraved on the lens.

items.producto: High-visibility reflective vest (mandatory equipment on motorcycles)
items.descripcion: From 1/10/2026 motorcycles must carry, as part of their mandatory equipment, a high-visibility reflective vest in accordance with PPE regulations (RD 518/2026, Annex XII of the General Vehicle Regulations; BOE-A-2026-13889). For the car, it is still what keeps you legal if you get out on foot along the hard shoulder at night.

secciones.intro: What you need if you have to spend the night in the car or walk to an exit.

items.descripcion: Compact version of the basic first-aid kit, adapted for road traffic accidents.
Retains 90% of body heat. Takes up the space of a pack of cigarettes.
Attaches to the hood or bodywork. Hands-free for nighttime breakdowns.
For being towed or towing using emergency straps.

items.producto: Snow chains or textile snow socks
items.descripcion: Textile or metal. Mandatory on signposted snowy sections.

secciones.intro: Water, some warmth and battery. On a snowy mountain pass or in a summer traffic jam, that is what keeps your spirits up.

items.descripcion: 20,000 mAh power bank: 4-5 full phone charges.
Replace every 6 months: the plastic degrades in the heat of the car.
Quick energy in a compact format. 400–500 kcal per bar.

kit-hogar.resumen: Home kit: 22 items for stay-at-home situations and household emergencies. Guide based on official sources (EU + Civil Protection).
kit-hogar.coste_total: 210-420 € (2 people, 7–10 days, with stove, light, radio, power bank and CO detector)
kit-hogar.paraQuien: For anyone who wants to be covered without having to leave home: water cuts, lockdowns, storms that isolate a neighborhood, or simply a week when you do not feel like or cannot go out to buy supplies. It is the pantry stock, not the backpack.
kit-hogar.paraQuien_no: It is not suitable for evacuation: if you have to leave in 15 minutes, this stays where it is. In that case, prepare the evacuation backpack with the essentials. And if you have a pet or baby, the stock must include their supplies from day one, not when you run out.

antes: Calculate water and food for everyone in the household × 3 days
If there are children, babies or pets: adjust the kit for them
Keep games or books on hand to keep morale up
Keep a manual can opener and a tested butane stove: without them, your canned food is useless
Fill at least one bathtub with water for non-potable use (toilet cisterns, cleaning) if the cut is imminent
Test the radio, flashlight and stove once a quarter and keep spare batteries of the same size: a kit with dead batteries is not a kit
Charge the power bank and check expiry dates every six months, on the same day you change the clocks: that way you will never forget
durante: Ration water if the supply is cut off
Ventilate daily if possible
Keep the official radio on at least twice a day
Open windows for 5 minutes every few hours to refresh the air: the build-up of CO2 makes you feel down and sluggish
If you light a butane stove, candle or brazier, do it with ventilation and with the CO detector running: indoors, combustion consumes oxygen and carbon monoxide gives no warning
Keep your phone in power-saving mode and data off; call when you have signal and reserve the power bank for the radio and flashlight
despues: Inventory of what has been consumed and immediate replacement
Replace batteries, water and food consumed the same day, not the following week: the next emergency gives no warning
Write down what you missed during those days: that list, and no other, is what you need to buy for the kit

errores: Buying things nobody in the house eats. An emergency pantry is rotated by eating it, and if you don't like it, it doesn't get rotated.
Not having a can opener: if you have 30 cans and can't open them, you don't have food, you have a set of gym weights.
Having no way to cook without electricity: twenty cans and a stove that is off.
Forgetting water for non-drinking use: without tap water you can't flush the toilet. Filling the bathtub in time is free.
Storing everything together in a single cupboard: if one room floods or is damaged, you lose the entire reserve.
Not adding the household's chronic medication to the plan: two weeks' reserve of treatment is the difference between holding out and having to go out.
Using your phone as a flashlight: the most expensive light is the one that leaves you without battery to make a call
Storing batteries inside the radio or flashlight: they corrode and ruin the device just when you need it. Store them separately, in their packaging

secciones.intro: The base of the pantry. A realistic amount for the days you want to cover, and rotation so it doesn't expire.

items.descripcion: Food-grade container for storing drinking water. Allow 3 litres per person per day.
Protein and calories without refrigeration. Prioritize legumes and fish.

items.producto: Pasta, rice and pulses in packets
items.descripcion: Long-shelf-life calorie base (2-3 years).
Don't forget them: an extra ration for at least 3 days.

secciones.intro: When water is scarce, hygiene is the first thing to break down and the second to make you ill.

items.descripcion: Basic hygiene without guaranteed running water.
DANA floodwater leaves mud mixed with sewage: disinfect everything.
If water fails, the toilet won't flush: manage waste with bags.
Without running water you can't flush the toilet or wash. Sealable bags to manage waste hygienically until the tap comes back.

secciones.intro: If the power goes out and you can't cook, the 20 cans in the cupboard are useless without a can opener. Always have a way to prepare hot food.

items.descripcion: Heat water and cook canned food and broth without electricity. Always use it in a ventilated area.
Without electricity, the electric can opener doesn't work. A manual one for 5 € is the most underrated tool in the kit.

items.producto: Sturdy cooking pot or saucepan (for heating canned food)
items.descripcion: You can heat empty cans with water and put the canned food inside (makeshift bain-marie) or use a saucepan to heat water if the power is out.

This kit recommends a butane stove indoors: CO has no smell, cannot be seen, and kills while you sleep. Place it at breathing height, in the kitchen or wherever you cook, and never turn it off to save batteries.

secciones.intro: Thermometer, antiseptic, general painkillers and whatever your doctor prescribes. With no pharmacy open, the first-aid kit is the pharmacy.

items.descripcion: To detect fever when you can't see a doctor immediately.
Basic painkillers and fever reducers. Check the expiry date annually.
Protection against dust, smoke or a respiratory outbreak.

secciones.intro: Three days without power with a child at home and nothing to do can feel very long. The psychological side also needs preparing.

items.descripcion: Morale matters: 72 hours shut in feel endless with nothing to do.
Entertainment without batteries or a network.

secciones.intro: Without forced ventilation during confinement, the air gets contaminated quickly. Two simple measures prevent headaches and fatigue.

items.descripcion: Keep the air moving if heat builds up. It runs on the kit's power bank for hours.

items.producto: Portable CO2 or air quality monitor
items.descripcion: CO2 build-up in a closed home makes you drowsy, gives you a headache and reduces your ability to think. A cheap sensor warns you.

secciones.intro: A shelter-in-place kit without light or radio relies on a phone that runs out of battery within hours. These three devices keep the home informed and lit when there is no mains power.

items.descripcion: Without light you can't find anything and end up using your phone as a flashlight—exactly what you need to make calls. Keep spare batteries of the same size, outside the devices.

When the mobile network goes down, the radio keeps broadcasting official alerts without internet or using your phone's battery. Tune in to local stations before storing it and test reception where you plan to use it.
With your phone at 20%, you have two calls left. A charged power bank gives you several full charges and powers the radio or fan via USB. Recharge it every six months even if you don't use it.

kit-montana.titulo: Mountain Kit: 15 essentials for outdoor survival (2026)
kit-montana.resumen: Mountain kit: 15 essentials for outdoor survival. Navigation, warmth, water and communication without a network. Practical guide 2026.
kit-montana.coste_total: 105-205 € (you probably already have much of it if you run or cycle)
kit-montana.paraQuien: For people who go hiking, canyoning or mountain skiing. 90% of mountain rescues in Spain involve people who got lost, injured or were caught out by nightfall. You don't need to be an expert: just going a little further than planned is enough.
kit-montana.paraQuien_no: It is not high-mountain gear: for glaciers, via ferrata or overnight stays at altitude you need technical equipment and training. And if you go to an area without coverage, this kit won't keep you in contact: phones don't always work, and the real solution is to tell someone your route and expected return time.

antes: Always share your route and return time with someone
Check the weather warning (AEMET) before you set out
Download the 112 app for your region
Never wear new footwear or socks for the first time on a long hike: 74% of pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago get blisters in the first few days (Colexio de Podólogos de Galicia)
durante: If you get lost, stay put and make yourself visible
Ration water and don't stray from the known route
Use trekking poles if possible: they reduce impact on knees and ankles by up to 30%
If you feel rubbing: stop and apply a hydrocolloid dressing before the blister forms (Compeed, Scholl or similar)
despues: Restock and check the kit after every outing
Note down what you were missing for next time
Dry and store the rain jacket: moisture leads to mold and it loses its waterproofing

errores: Going out in city clothes and trusting the weather app. In the mountains, the temperature drops 10 degrees going up a ravine, and fog can arrive in 20 minutes.
A single flashlight for the group, with no spare batteries, at the bottom of the backpack.
Not carrying an extra warm layer “because I'm doing the route in two hours”: half an hour waiting for a rescue in a gully is spent at zero degrees.
Drinking little and arriving at the end dehydrated and with heatstroke, especially in spring with sun and a backpack.
Relying on your phone to navigate. It runs out of battery, gets dropped, gets wet. Map and compass, and know how to use them before you need them.

items.descripcion: 3 liters in 92 g. It fits into any gap in the backpack and takes up no space when empty. It accepts 42 mm screw-on filters (Katadyn BeFree) and withstands hot water up to 60 °C.
They turn stream or spring water into drinking water in 30 minutes, with no filter or battery.

secciones.intro: Knowing where you are and being able to call for help. A whistle can be heard much farther than your voice and doesn't tire you out. Add paracord for lashing and improvisation.

items.descripcion: 20,000 mAh power bank: 4-5 full phone charges.
It can be heard 1 km away; your voice, 100 meters. No battery.

items.producto: Physical map and compass for the area
items.descripcion: Classic navigation doesn't fail. Learn to use it before you set out.
4 mm cord, 250 kg strength. It can be used to lash a backpack, improvise shelter, immobilize an injury or help another hiker. It is not for climbing.

secciones.intro: What prevents hypothermia if you are forced to stop and wait for hours.

items.descripcion: Dual-sided: orange to be seen, silver to retain heat.
Hypothermia kills in the mountains, even in summer.
30% of body heat is lost through the head.

secciones.intro: Buckles, cuts, blisters and broken gear: the trail's minor surgery.

items.descripcion: Bandages, adhesive tape, blister care, basic immobilisation supplies.

items.producto: Sunscreen and lip balm with SPF
items.descripcion: SPF 50: radiation in the mountains is much higher than at the beach.
64% of hikers' medical visits are for blisters. Apply them at the first sign of rubbing, before the blister appears. Compeed or similar.
Cuts, saws, opens cans and repairs gear. The hiker's Swiss Army knife.
Needles, thread and mini scissors in a compact case. To fix your backpack, your clothes or a rain jacket torn mid-trail.
Hands-free for walking at night or repairing gear.

kit-calor.titulo: Heat Kit / Heatwave: 7 items that save lives (2026)
kit-calor.resumen: Heat kit: 7 items that save lives in a heatwave — hydration, cooling and sun protection. From 30 €, and you probably already have most of them.
kit-calor.coste_total: 30-70 € (you probably already have most of it)
kit-calor.paraQuien: For homes without air conditioning or with power cuts during a heatwave, and for anyone with older people, babies or chronically ill people at home. Spain spends weeks above 40 degrees and heatwaves are the natural hazard that causes the most deaths, almost all of them preventable.
kit-calor.paraQuien_no: It's not a beach or hiking kit: there, what matters is shade, a hat and water. Nor does it replace real prevention: if your home reaches 35 degrees at night, the kit helps, but the plan is to go somewhere cool.

antes: Close blinds and sunny windows during the day
Drink water even if you're not thirsty; avoid alcohol and caffeine
Check on older neighbours and vulnerable people

Follow AEMET warnings and ES-Alert alerts on your phone: the Basic Directive on adverse weather phenomena (BOE, 27/04/2026) establishes them as the main warning channel. The National Action Plan for Excess Temperatures is active from 1 June to 15 September
durante: Stay in the coolest room in the home
Lukewarm showers, not cold
If you feel dizzy, have a headache or hot, dry skin: it could be heatstroke, call 112
despues: Check whether anyone's medication needs refrigeration and have a plan B

errores: Drinking lots of plain water on days of heavy sweating, without salts. Hyponatremia (low salt) causes dizziness and confusion and is mistaken for heatstroke itself.
Lowering the blind late. When the house is already at 33 degrees, opening south- and west-facing windows lets the heat in.
Leaving someone in a parked car: the interior rises by more than 20 degrees in 15 minutes. Pets too.
Relying on a fan when it's above 35 degrees: it moves hot air around and dehydrates you. Beyond that point you need to cool the body, not the air.
Ignoring the older person who lives alone and says they're fine. Heatstroke in older people causes confusion, not thirst: they don't ask for help.

secciones.intro: Cooling the body without electricity: towels, battery-powered fans and a spray bottle are worth more than they seem.

items.descripcion: Moves air when the heat is stifling. Works with a power bank.
Wet it and it lowers body temperature through evaporation. Reusable.
Sprays cold water onto the skin: immediate relief for mild heatstroke.

secciones.intro: Water plus salts, and knowing how much. An insulated bottle with ice in the morning gives you cold water at night.

items.producto: Steel insulated bottle (keeps cold for 12-24 h)
items.descripcion: Keeps water cold for 12-24 h even at 40 degrees.
They replenish mineral salts lost through sweat. What drinking water alone doesn't fix.

secciones.intro: Sunglasses, hat and sunscreen. The burns on day 2 of a heatwave are from having gone out for 20 minutes 'to run an errand'.

items.descripcion: Severe burns dehydrate you even more. Reapply every 2 hours.
Real UV protection, not cosmetic. Your eyes can burn too.

kit-evacuacion.titulo: Evacuation Kit: 14 items to get out alive (2026)
kit-evacuacion.resumen: Evacuation kit: 14 items to get out alive. Lightweight backpack with the essentials ready in 30 seconds. Quick preparation 2026.
kit-evacuacion.paraQuien: For when they tell you «get out of your house now» — a fire, a chemical explosion, a flash flood — and you come back in 3 days, or in a month. It's the only thing you carry in your hands, so decide now what goes inside, not when the alarm sounds.
kit-evacuacion.paraQuien_no: It's not the holiday suitcase or the long-stay kit: it's designed to get you through 72 hours away from home, not to live for a week in a sports hall. And if you have reduced mobility, a large pet or a baby, this backpack has to be split up and tested beforehand.

antes: Backpack in the hallway, always in the same spot
Copy of documents in a waterproof bag
Evacuation route agreed with the family
Spare house keys in the backpack: in a panic it's the first thing people forget
Test the backpack by walking 5 km with everything inside: that's the only way to know whether it carries well and what you're missing
durante: Don't go back home for forgotten items
Follow only the instructions of the emergency services
If you have to move on foot, wear closed, comfortable shoes: the ground may be covered in glass and debris

If you evacuate at night or with poor visibility along an interurban road, wear the reflective element: from 1/10/2026 it is mandatory for pedestrians on the roadway or hard shoulder (RD 518/2026, art. 123, BOE-A-2026-13889)
despues: Do not enter the home until officially authorised
Always wear protective footwear and gloves when handling debris: mud and debris after a flood or fire can be contaminated
Check the backpack every 6 months: update medication, food and expired documents

errores: Leaving it in the storage room or in the car: if you are being evacuated at night from bed, the backpack has to be in the hallway, hanging up, with everything inside.
Packing clothes for a month. It weighs 12 kilos, your shoulders hurt at 4 km and you end up dropping things along the way. 30-40 L and under 8 kg.
Not testing it: walk 5 kilometres with it one Sunday. It's the only way to know what you're missing and what's too much.
Not including a copy of your keys, your documents and a prepaid phone card that doesn't depend on your own line.
Forgetting small notes and a charger: in the first days, the queue to charge your phone is the most repeated scene of any disaster.

secciones.intro: What can't be replaced for months: ID card, deeds, policies, medical cards, on paper and on USB.

items.producto: Waterproof folder or sleeve for documents (ID card, deeds, policies, prescriptions)
items.descripcion: ID card, deeds, policies, health card and prescriptions all in one place.

items.producto: Digital copy on an encrypted USB drive
items.descripcion: Backup of scanned documents. Encrypt it with a password.
A copy kept in the waterproof folder. In the panic of an evacuation, it's the first thing people forget: you go back home and can't open the door.

secciones.intro: Water, food, warmth and a place to shelter while you are relocated.

items.descripcion: Water-resistant, with a padded belt. It will keep you going for 3 days.
They purify questionable water in 30 minutes. Vital if bottled water runs out.
At least 2 rations per person in the backpack.
A minimal combo for warmth and rain protection.

secciones.intro: Radio to find out what's going on, light to move around, knife and whistle to repair and call for help, first-aid kit for treating injuries, and cash to buy when everything is cash.

items.descripcion: Minimal power kit: to see and communicate.
Mini but complete version: gauze, antiseptic, painkillers.
During an evacuation, ATMs don't work. 10-20 € banknotes.
The only source of information if internet and phone networks go down. With a dynamo so it never goes silent.
Three whistles are the international emergency signal. It carries farther than your voice and never runs out. Essential if you get trapped.
23 tools in a compact body: knife, saw, screwdrivers, bottle opener. Just what you need for emergency repairs.

items.producto: Light or reflective item for walking at night (mandatory for pedestrians)
items.descripcion: As of 1/10/2026, anyone walking on the roadway or shoulder of an interurban road between sunset and sunrise, or in reduced visibility, must carry at least one luminous or reflective element in accordance with PPE regulations, visible at 150 m (RD 518/2026, art. 123 of the General Traffic Regulations, BOE-A-2026-13889). In a nighttime evacuation after a DANA or wildfire, it is the difference between being seen or not.

huerto-autosuficiencia.resumen: Self-sufficient garden: 13 tools to produce your food: seeds, compost, autonomous irrigation and protection. From €50 to get started; €300 fully set up.
huerto-autosuficiencia.coste_total: €50-200 to start well (seeds, growing medium, trays, tools) — up to €300 with compost bin, netting and irrigation.
huerto-autosuficiencia.paraQuien: For those who want the next step: stop depending on the shopping cart and understand where the food they eat comes from. Starting with a balcony of sprouts is realistic, cheap and hooks you. It is also your food insurance: a few kilos of well-stored seeds provide food for a year.
huerto-autosuficiencia.paraQuien_no: It is not a real self-sufficiency plan for a family on its own: living from a garden requires soil, water, time and two or three years of learning. And if you don't even have somewhere to put a pot, set up the basic kit first: it's more urgent and cheaper.

antes: Observe your space: how many hours of direct sun it gets per day (4 h minimum for tomatoes, 2-3 h is enough for lettuce and herbs)
Start with what is easy and productive: lettuce, arugula, chard, herbs, radishes
Prepare the calendar: in Spain, spring sowing runs from February to April; autumn for spinach, garlic and onion
Set up a household compost bin: kitchen scraps feed the garden. A 20 L bucket with a tap costs €25-35 and prevents odors
Cover windows with anti-aphid netting (2x8 m, €10-20): without protection, whiteflies and thrips destroy a balcony garden in two weeks

Check your homeowners' association rules or housing portal: some buildings (especially rentals) prohibit pots on balconies or communal terraces. If they allow them, ask about maximum weight and watering.
Buy pots with a saucer: the saucer catches the irrigation water and prevents stains on the floor of the entrance or shared terrace. Without a saucer, nobody will let you keep the garden.
durante: Water early in the morning or at dusk, never in direct sun
Loose, well-draining growing medium: a pot without holes is certain death for any plant
Feed every 2-3 weeks with compost or liquid fertilizer
If you use drip irrigation, check the drippers every week: they clog easily and a dry plant goes unnoticed until it's too late
Check the aphid netting after storms: if it's torn, replace it. A 2 cm hole is enough for whitefly to get in
If you grow in pots, renew the growing medium every season: after one season it has lost nutrients and become compacted. About 5-8 € per pot and two new harvests.
despues: Harvest from the outside (outer leaves) so the plant keeps producing
Save seeds from your best plants for the next cycle
Note down what worked and what didn't: your garden notebook is your best tool

errores: Starting with 20 varieties and a big garden. It gets abandoned in six weeks. Start with three things you actually eat: tomato, lettuce, herbs.
Sowing when the calendar says so instead of when your climate says so: sow when your valley's temperature allows it, not when the table says so.
Using cheap growing medium from the discount store or garden soil in pots: it compacts, doesn't drain and you kill the roots.
Not having water secured: in a balcony garden, a weekend away without watering is a dead garden.
Storing seeds without drying them and without a date: after two years nothing germinates. Airtight jar, label, cool dark place.

Throwing kitchen scraps in the bin: a 20 L compost bin costs less than 35 € and turns that waste into free fertilizer. The right ratio is two parts browns (dry leaves, cardboard) to one part greens (food scraps).
Relying on insecticides without netting: whitefly reproduces in two weeks and insecticides kill bees. Cover first, treat afterwards.

secciones.intro: Seeds, trays, growing medium and a measuring jug. For less than 60 € you get half a year of salads, sprouts and well-watered cherry tomatoes.

items.descripcion: Tomato, pepper, eggplant, zucchini and more, with certified organic seeds. The best starting point.
Seed starter trays to get strong plants going before moving them to pots. Reusable, recyclable material.
Soil with fertiliser already mixed in, works for practically any vegetable grown in a pot.

secciones.intro: Three quality pieces are worth more than a fifteen-piece case that falls apart.

items.descripcion: Rake, transplanter and hoe from a long-established Spanish brand. Just the essentials.

items.producto: 6 L watering can with detachable rose
items.descripcion: Soft rose for seedlings and a direct stream for mature plants.

secciones.intro: A mini greenhouse and some reading for when you have already killed your first tomato and want to understand why. With compost and watering, the vegetable patch goes from hobby to real production.

items.descripcion: Extends the season and protects from the cold on a balcony or terrace. Fits in any corner.

items.producto: Urban and organic vegetable garden manual for beginners
items.descripcion: From zero to a full vegetable garden: how to turn a terrace or garden into food, step by step.
The reference illustrated guide: sowing calendar, companion planting, pests.

kit-30-dias.titulo: 30-Day Kit: 16 items for a month without supplies (2026)
kit-30-dias.resumen: 30-Day Kit: 16 items for a month without supplies — 180 L of water for 2, pantry food, cooking and looking after yourself without power. 300-500 € that pays for itself as you eat it.
kit-30-dias.coste_total: 300-500 € (2 people, and much of it pays for itself as you eat it)
kit-30-dias.paraQuien: For anyone who has the 72 hours covered and wants to take the leap: a week without being able to buy anything, a region cut off by a DANA, a long blackout or a lockdown-type episode. Here there is no backpack any more — there is a pantry and a plan.
kit-30-dias.paraQuien_no: It is nobody's first kit: if you do not have the 72-hour one set up, start there — it covers 95% of real scenarios and costs a fraction. And with 30 days you do not get 30 days of medical autonomy or endless water: work out how to get water and how to reach a doctor before stockpiling food.

antes: Work out real consumption: 2 people, 30 days = 60 L of drinking water + 40-60 L for basic hygiene
Prioritise food you already eat: an emergency pantry you never rotate is money down the drain
Store everything in a cool, dark, dry place; write the purchase date on every pack
Add what is specific to your household to your kit: regular medication, nappies, pet food
durante: Start eating by use-by date: fridge first, then freezer (it stays cold for 24-48 h if you keep it closed), then the pantry
Ration water per person, not per day: 3 L/day per adult for drinking is the minimum
Use the stove in a ventilated area, never inside a closed room
despues: Replace what you have used the following week, writing the dates again
Check that tins are not bulging or rusty and replace them
Note what was left over and what ran out: adjust quantities for the next check

errores: Buying 30 days of food and not being able to cook it: with no gas or power, raw rice is just decoration. Secure a way to cook and fuel first.
Not calculating water: 3 L per person per day is 180 L for two people for a month. It is the first thing to run out and the thing that takes up the most space.
Not rotating. A pantry you never touch is rubbish within three years; one you eat from day to day never expires.
Not counting the bathroom: without water, 96 rolls fall short and hygiene becomes the household's health problem.
Doing it all at once and at the worst price. Build it over 4-6 months by adding two packs per shop, and that way it costs half as much.

secciones.intro: The real bottleneck of the month. Large containers with a tap, rotation and a plan for making water safe to drink.

items.producto: 8 L jugs with dispensing tap (x8 = 64 L)
items.descripcion: Bezoya 8 L with tap: handy for measuring out. Allow 3 L/day per person for drinking and cooking.
The jug from your local supermarket works just as well. Also store bathwater if there is advance warning.

secciones.intro: What keeps you going: tins and ready meals that can be eaten cold and need no cooking.

items.producto: Tuna in spring water (pack of 6 tins)
items.descripcion: Cheap, long-lasting protein. Multiply packs according to the days covered.

items.producto: Litoral lentils a la riojana (pack of 6)
items.descripcion: Complete ready-to-eat dish, can be eaten cold if there is no way to heat it.
Calories and protein in a single tub. Very good energy-to-price ratio.

items.producto: Assorted Galician canned specialties (12 gourmet cans)
items.descripcion: Mussels, sardines, cockles… varying the flavor keeps morale up in a long crisis.
Easy to eat without cooking, on toast or on its own. Long shelf life.

secciones.intro: Rice, pasta, legumes and powdered milk. Cheap, calorie-dense and with years of shelf life.

items.descripcion: The quintessential long-life food. Buy 6-8 kg for the month.
Makes ~7 liters of milk per bag. Vitamin D and calcium without a fridge.

secciones.intro: The cooking method is what turns a pantry into hot meals. Always in a ventilated area.

items.producto: 2-in-1 camping stove (large gas cylinder or cartridge)
items.descripcion: Takes a standard butane gas cylinder or a small cartridge. Use only in a ventilated area.
For cold during a winter blackout. Triple safety system. Always ventilate.
If the house becomes uninhabitable or to isolate a room and retain body heat.

secciones.intro: Paper, soap, a full first-aid kit and vitamins. What sustains health and morale for weeks.

items.descripcion: Dressings, bandages, antiseptics, gloves, adhesive tape. The 30-day health foundation.
It's one of the first things to disappear from supermarkets at any alert.
Covers deficiencies if your emergency diet is monotonous (no fresh fruit or vegetables).
A superfood dense in protein and micronutrients, with an extremely long shelf life.

kit-bebe.titulo: Baby Kit: 32 essentials to protect your child (2026)
kit-bebe.resumen: Baby kit: 32 emergency items — food without power, hygiene, warm clothing and documents. From 90 €; you already have almost everything: rotate, don't duplicate.
kit-bebe.coste_total: 90-170 € (much of it is what you already use every day: rotate it, don't duplicate it)
kit-bebe.paraQuien: Households with babies aged 0-18 months, and also anyone expecting one: it can be put together in two afternoons and pays for itself in everyday use. If you breastfeed, much of this kit is extra peace of mind; if not, it's essential.
kit-bebe.paraQuien_no: If the child already eats everything on their own, the basic kit plus two or three things from here (snacks, entertainment, warm clothing) is enough. This kit is designed for infants, not older children.

antes: Write down the baby's medication schedule/feeding plan and your pediatrician's phone number on a piece of paper: in an emergency, not knowing what they are taking is a problem
Keep a bottle and a sippy cup that you never use: they are spares, so they are not in the dishwasher the day you need them
Store photocopies of the baby's ID/health book and vaccination record in the waterproof pouch
Talk to your family: who takes the baby if you have to evacuate quickly? Decide roles now

Write the opening date on the lid of the formula can and set a reminder for 25 days: once opened it is used within about 4 weeks (as stated by the manufacturer), it does not last until the printed expiry date. Rotating it is what makes the kit useful.
durante: With a baby in your arms, the evacuation backpack is split: someone carries the child, you carry the little one's 24-hour bag
If you don't know whether you will be able to breastfeed calmly, express milk with a manual pump in the first days so you don't lose supply
Watch the baby's temperature: without power there is no room thermometer, feeling the back of the neck and chest is misleading, use the thermometer from the first-aid kit
Doubtful water for the bottle: boiling is not always possible — treat it and let it cool, or use low-mineral bottled water kept in reserve for infant feeding

Powdered formula: prepare it just before the feed (AESAN recommends consuming it within 2 hours) and throw away what is left in the bottle the baby has already drunk from. With ready-to-feed liquid formula you don't have that clock.

With no way to boil: sterilize with cold-water sterilizing tablets and rinse with safe drinking water. And if the baby is under 28 days old, was born premature or with low birth weight, AESAN indicates boiled water and adding powder when the water is above 70 °C (check the label and ask your pediatrician).
despues: Check for bumps and frights: babies cannot verbalize, any odd change in behavior or sleep, see the pediatrician
Restock what you use the same day: a diaper and milk supply that is not replenished is a half-finished kit
If the crisis was long, ask your health center to check the vaccination record and bring it up to date if needed

Restock with the current size and dose, not the kit's: babies change every month. And if during those days there was fever, vomiting or fewer wet diapers than usual, tell your pediatrician before considering the episode over.

errores: Not having BACKUP FORMULA: milk supply drops under stress and without 2-3 days of formula, that doubles the anxiety. Even if you breastfeed, put 400-800 g of formula on the list.
Relying on always being able to boil water: without gas or electricity you can't sterilize bottles — you need a dedicated safe-water bag and a cup, not just a bottle.
Not counting diapers: a baby uses 6-8 diapers a day. 72 hours is ~20 diapers: a small bag that almost nobody packs.
Storing the new puree that the baby has never tried: in an emergency you try food you already know they tolerate.
Forgetting the 'next size up' coat: babies grow and the coat set in the kit becomes too small at 3 months without anyone noticing.

Storing the bottle the baby didn't finish for the next feed. With powdered formula you throw away what's left: it's the most common mistake in an emergency and the one that causes the most gastroenteritis in a baby.
Leaving liquid formula in the car trunk or storage room: heat degrades it before the expiry date. Powder, however, does not go in the fridge (humidity makes it clump): cool and dry, not cold.

secciones.intro: Bottle and puree need safe water and temperature. Without electricity or gas, you get that with your own supply and a small butane heater.

items.producto: Low-sodium water for formula feeding (6 × 1.5 L pack)
items.descripcion: To prepare bottles without purifying water: look for low mineralization (sodium <20 mg/L), the type recommended for infants.
Plan B for tap or rainwater when bottled water runs out. Use only with clear water and allow the resting time.

items.producto: Bottle warmer without gas or electricity (chemical/self-heating)
items.descripcion: Bags that heat a bottle in minutes without fire. For warm puree and water at temperature in a car or a sports center.
Keeps hot water for mixing puree or warming the bottle for hours. Wide neck: easy to clean and fill with a spoon.
Safe cold water for the baby during a heatwave, and to keep expressed milk for a few hours if there's no fridge.

secciones.intro: Even if you breastfeed: stress and exhaustion can lower your supply right when there's nowhere to buy. The backup is insurance, not a doubt about your breastfeeding.

items.descripcion: A 2-3 day supply even if you breastfeed. Check the expiry date every 6 months and rotate it by using it in porridge or cooking.
Made with lukewarm or cold water, they go a long way and need no cooking. The one your baby already takes: don't try a new brand in an emergency.
Real food without cooking, with a long shelf life. If they already eat purées, these are your kit and their dinner in a blackout.
No batteries or electricity needed, it keeps your supply up and prevents painful engorgement if the baby can't latch well (on the floor, in the car, in a field hospital).
For expressing and storing with a date. Without a freezer, they last a few hours in a cool bag with ice packs.

secciones.intro: When running water is gone, baby hygiene is the first thing that gets complicated. Everything in this section fits in a 5-liter waterproof bag.

items.descripcion: 6-8 a day: 20 diapers is 3 days. Write the size and date on the bag; the baby will outgrow the size before you move house.
Double duty: diaper and face without water. In an emergency you use more than you think: close the pack well or they dry out in a week.

items.producto: Waterproof bags for dirty clothes and diapers (pack)
items.descripcion: One for dirty, one for clean clothes. With no washing machine and a child, keeping clean and dirty apart is worth gold.
A clean, padded place to change the baby when you have no home: washable Oxford fabric, folds into a pocket. In a shelter or a car, it makes a difference.
With a diaper all day and limited water, rash appears within 48 h and everyone sleeps badly.
It goes further than liquid soap with little water and also works for washing bottles and little hands.

secciones.intro: A baby loses heat five times faster than an adult. With no light or heating, this is the section that prevents an emergency.

items.producto: Warm one-piece sleep sack/pajamas (current size + one spare)
items.descripcion: Better than loose blankets: it won't come off while they sleep, and it leaves your hands free for carrying.

items.producto: Baby emergency thermal blanket (or a small fleece blanket)
items.descripcion: Don't leave the silver thermal blanket loose near the face: use it under the normal blanket or as a wind barrier in the carrycot.

The hat is for outdoors and for an evacuation, not for sleeping. The NHS recommends keeping the room at 16–20 °C and not overheating the baby: when you come indoors, hat off. Mittens are for carrying the baby in cold weather.

items.producto: Ergonomic baby carrier (sling or Mei Tai)
items.descripcion: Hands free for the flashlight, the backpack and the door. In an evacuation, a baby carrier is worth more than a stroller: there are no elevators or sidewalks.

secciones.intro: The baby first-aid kit plus what keeps a small child's spirits up for 48 hours shut in or in a strange place.

items.descripcion: Yours will do, but keep one dedicated: with no light and a fright, being able to take a temperature in 10 seconds saves a night of doubt.

With vomiting or diarrhea from bad water, dehydration in babies progresses quickly: early hydration and see the pediatrician. Nebulizer saline (hypertonic saline) is not for drinking; this is oral rehydration, with the WHO formulation. Follow your pediatrician's or nurse's guidance, not the internet.
Babies can't blow their noses: when congested they don't eat or sleep. And saline is also useful for eyes, wounds and general cleaning.

items.producto: Small favorite toys (2-3, in a waterproof bag)
items.descripcion: The usual ones, not new ones: in a strange place with strange lights, familiar things are what calms the baby.
That little blanket that smells of home. If it gets lost in an evacuation, it's a three-hour drama: keep an identical one in the kit.

secciones.intro: The baby doesn't carry an ID card, can't say their name, and doesn't have their own health card visible. Their whole identity fits in a waterproof pouch.

items.producto: Waterproof bag for the baby's documents (ID, health record, passport)
items.descripcion: Photocopies + originals inside a waterproof bag. With a small child and no network, a piece of paper with their date of birth and allergies goes a long way.

items.producto: Child ID card (name, date of birth, blood type, allergies, contacts)
items.descripcion: A laminated card in the backpack and a recent printed photo of the child. If you are separated during an evacuation, this is what identifies them.

items.producto: Recent printed photos of the baby and the family
items.descripcion: It sounds old-fashioned and it works: at a reception center, a photo in a wallet is worth more than a phone with no battery.

kit-mayores.titulo: Senior Kit: 27 items to protect dependents (2026)
kit-mayores.resumen: Senior kit: 27 items for dependent people — chronic medication, assistive devices, fall prevention and adapted food. From 60 €, not including prescription.
kit-mayores.coste_total: 60-120 € (not including the medication itself, which requires a prescription)
kit-mayores.paraQuien: Households with people aged 70 or over, especially if they live alone, take chronic medication or rely on hearing aids, glasses or assisted mobility. A family member assembles it in an afternoon and reviews it with the prescription folder.
kit-mayores.paraQuien_no: It does not replace telecare or the caregiver plan: it is materials, not a service. And if the person requires daily healthcare (oxygen, dialysis), the plan is discussed with their health center, not with this list.

antes: Make the medical ID card together with the person: conditions, medication with doses, allergies, doctor, contacts. Renew it every 6 months during the review.
Ask the doctor or nurse for a 2-week plan of chronic medication: in Spain, the electronic prescription allows most treatments to be collected in advance; your doctor will tell you how.
Practice using the card and the telecare phone with the person, not just in front of them: in an emergency, 'they already know' is not enough.
Agree with neighbors and family who calls whom and what warning signal you use (call, message, knocking on the wall: during power cuts some people use a whistle).

Count how many times they get up at night to use the bathroom: if it is more than once, a commode with a handle, a night light in the hallway and a non-slip mat come before any other product on the list.
Store medication in a bag with a handle that the person can hang over their shoulder, not in stacked boxes: in a quick exit, you only grab what you can pick up with one hand.
durante: Medication first: if you have to decide, chronic treatment is not skipped; the kit's reserve is for exactly that.
With hearing aids out of batteries or broken glasses, the person becomes isolated and disoriented: check that they can hear and see before anything else.
Heat or cold: older people regulate temperature worse and do not notice thirst. In a heatwave without power, keep water in sight and set a drinking schedule, even if they don't ask.
Do not let them make decisions alone if they are confused: heatstroke and dehydration cause confusion before weakness.

Without a washing machine or hot water, incontinence is the day-2 problem: use absorbent pads and a separate bag for soiled clothes. Do not hand-wash with the reserve water: that water is for drinking.

If the phone fails and she lives alone, a whistle and rhythmic knocks on the wall are how a neighbor can locate her. Agree it in advance with the neighbor and with her, using a specific signal (three knocks, pause, three knocks).
despues: Check medication that has been used and restock the kit the same day with the prescription.
Check hearing aid batteries, pacemaker batteries if applicable, and flashlights: in the scare, many things get used without being replaced.
Talk to the health center if treatment was interrupted: sometimes it has to be prescribed again.
Encourage them to talk about what they experienced: after a long emergency, an older person's emotional crash is as real as a burst pipe.

Check the skin in folds and pressure areas if there has been more than 24 hours without being able to wash: an irritation or a red area that does not recover should be discussed with their nurse or doctor, not treated at home.
Note down which product was actually missing and restock it that same day: the kit is corrected with what was used, not with what you thought you would use.

errores: Not having 2 weeks' supply of chronic medication in reserve. It is THE mistake: after a disaster, the pharmacy opens late or does not open, and stopping anticoagulants, antihypertensives or insulin is an emergency.
Forgetting hearing aid batteries: without hearing, the person does not hear the radio, does not understand the warning and does not ask for help. A blister pack of spare batteries in every kit.
Relying on the mobile phone: small screens, small print and no one to help them dial. The landline still works without electricity (analog ones do) and paper contacts never run out.
Not preparing for the fall: without light, a carpeted hallway with no night light means a broken hip. LED night lights cost €10 and prevent 50% of that scenario.
Storing everything in the high kitchen cupboard. If you evacuate, the older adult's 24-hour bag must be within easy reach, with name and contacts.

Not planning for incontinence. Without a washing machine or hot water, a single day without enough spare pads forces a choice between hygiene and drinking water. €15-30 in the cupboard solves it long before it's needed.

secciones.intro: The heart of this kit. Three things: a 2-4 week supply, a copy of the dosing instructions, and a way to keep what needs cold cold.

items.producto: Weekly pill organizer (pillbox) with a copy of dosing instructions
items.descripcion: Filled from the kit's supply. If someone else has to give the medication, the pillbox plus the record sheet prevent mistakes.
Name, allergies, medication, and emergency contact engraved on the metal, in plain sight for anyone treating you. A paper card gets wet; this doesn't.

items.producto: Small cool box with reusable ice packs
items.descripcion: For insulin and medication that must stay cold: with spare frozen packs it holds for 24-36 h. Check with your pharmacist which medication needs it.
2-4 degrees or in the bin. A €4 thermometer tells you whether the insulin is still good after the blackout.

items.producto: Water purification tablet and measuring cup for medication
items.descripcion: For taking pills with safe, measured water. A small detail you'll be grateful for on day 2.

items.producto: Battery-powered upper-arm blood pressure monitor with memory
items.descripcion: If someone at home has diagnosed hypertension, the plug-in model is useless in a blackout. This one runs on batteries and stores recent readings so you can write them on the record sheet. What values are normal and when to measure is for your doctor or nurse to decide: only the device belongs here.

secciones.intro: Hearing aids, glasses, pacemaker, prostheses: if these fail, everything else in the kit stops being useful, because the person can't hear the warning or see the door.

items.producto: Spare hearing aid batteries (blister pack × 3, with date)
