items.descripcion: Hearing aids run down and batteries expire. Sealed blister pack with the date written on it: no batteries, no hearing, no communication.
An old pair in good condition or the prescription written down to order another pair. They get dropped and break right then; with the prescription in the drawer, half an hour with an online optician.

items.producto: Denture box + adhesive and cup with lid
items.descripcion: If they wear dentures: without spare adhesive and without a cup to keep them in overnight, they can't eat. A detail nobody considers.

items.producto: Folding cane / spare walker with light
items.descripcion: The cane stays in the other room when you need it. A lightweight one in the hallway with a built-in night light.

items.producto: Alert bracelet: pacemaker or implanted device
items.descripcion: A healthcare professional needs to know before a defibrillator or an MRI. Engraved and visible on the wrist, it works even if you can't speak.

items.producto: Engraved medical ID bracelet or necklace (name, phone number, allergies)
items.descripcion: With cognitive impairment or disorientation, in an evacuation the first thing to get lost is the wallet with the papers. An engraved bracelet or necklace with name, a relative's phone number and allergies can be read without unlocking anything or opening any pocket, and it doesn't expire or run out of battery.

secciones.intro: A blackout doesn't kill an elderly person: the rug in the dark and the bathroom at night do. 20 € on a night light and a non-slip mat change the prognosis.

items.producto: LED night lights with sensor (pack of 2-3)
items.descripcion: They plug into the hallway and bathroom sockets and run on an internal battery: when the power is out, they light up without pressing anything. A nighttime fall is THE preventable accident.
The big, easy kind, not the small one in the drawer: with clumsy hands or in the dark, it should be easy to find and switch on by itself.

items.producto: Non-slip bath mat and support grab rail
items.descripcion: Without hot water and with buckets in the way, the bathroom becomes an ice rink. 20 € and an afternoon of DIY.
If they can't shout or the mobile phone doesn't work, a whistle is heard through walls much more than a voice. Teach them to use it beforehand.

secciones.intro: That they can call for help and that someone knows they are alone. Half the danger for an elderly person in an emergency is that nobody misses them for hours.

items.producto: Battery-powered FM radio with high volume and a large dial
items.descripcion: Official information without relying on a mobile phone. Practise using it once a month so it isn't an unfamiliar object.

items.producto: Paper contact sheet in large print (112, family, doctor, neighbour, pharmacy)
items.descripcion: Stuck on the fridge and on the bedside table. A phone with numbers pre-dialled is no use if they don't know how to unlock it or can't find it.

items.producto: Neighbourhood agreement with a check-in call/knock
items.descripcion: A designated neighbour calls or drops by every morning during a crisis. It isn't an object; it's the most effective measure on the whole list: write it down on the card.
No screens and no battery: half an hour of play changes the mood of a long afternoon. Large print for anyone who can't see up close.

secciones.intro: Without a washing machine and hot water, what at home is solved with one wash becomes the problem of day 2. Here are the three things that protect an older person's dignity and skin best when services are down.

items.producto: Incontinence underpads and adult diapers (pack for 3–5 days)
items.descripcion: If there is incontinence, it's the first thing to run out and the last thing you can improvise: without a washing machine, hot water and with the bathroom in darkness, there's no home-made replacement. Size and absorbency should be adjusted with their nurse or at the pharmacy, not by eye.

items.producto: Bedpan or urinal with a handle
items.descripcion: With reduced mobility or no light, the nighttime trip to the bathroom is the expected fall. A bedpan with a handle and a night light are enough so they don't have to get up in the dark. Empty and clean it with cleaning water, never with the reserved drinking water.

Older people lose heat faster and notice it less. The gold blanket doesn't give off heat by itself: it reflects body heat. It works much better inside a normal blanket, not alone on top. It costs less than a coffee and fits in any drawer.

secciones.intro: Without a kitchen, without knives and sometimes without dentures: the person must be able to eat the food in the kit as their mouth and strength allow.

items.producto: Ready soft food (purées, adult purée jars, tubs of creamy food)
items.descripcion: If they have chewing problems, canned food is no good: purées and adult purée jars in cups, eaten on their own.
Calories and protein without cooking or chewing. In a 3-day crisis, this is what maintains an older person's weight.

items.producto: Liquid thickeners (if dysphagia has been diagnosed)
items.descripcion: People with dysphagia swallow air when drinking from a cup and choke in an emergency. Follow their speech therapist/doctor's guidance: this is only prescribed by their professional.

items.producto: Bottle with handle and easy-drink spout + cup with lid
items.descripcion: Drinking unaided, without spilling, with one hand. Dehydration in older people appears without thirst: keep water in front of them and easy to reach.

kit-mascotas.titulo: Pet Kit: 23 items to protect your animal (2026)
kit-mascotas.resumen: Pet kit: 23 items to protect your animal in emergencies. Food, identification and first aid.
kit-mascotas.coste_total: 40-90 € (20-40 € if you already have a carrier and bowl)
kit-mascotas.paraQuien: For any home with a dog or cat. In an evacuation due to fire, flood or smoke, the animal cannot stay and there is not always room for it: the difference between taking it with you and losing it is having the carrier and leash findable in 30 seconds.
kit-mascotas.paraQuien_no: It is not a kit for leaving the animal alone at home for three days: an animal cannot manage itself like a pantry. If your emergency plan involves leaving it behind, that plan does not work.

antes: Keep the carrier and leash in the same place as your emergency backpack, not in the storage room
Calculate water: about 50-60 ml per kilo per day (a 15 kg dog drinks almost 1 litre a day; a cat, 200-300 ml)
Keep a paper copy of the health record and microchip number: they ask for it at shelters or refuges
Take a recent photo of the animal with you and save it on your phone and on paper: it is what proves it is yours
If your dog needs a muzzle because of a potentially dangerous breed, keep it next to the leash: without it they will not let you take it on certain types of transport
durante: Animals sense fear: speak normally, do not pick it up if it is large, put it in the carrier without a fuss
Offer water every 2-3 hours; stress dehydrates more than heat
Do not improvise with human food: sudden diet changes cause diarrhoea just when there is no vet
If there is smoke or gas, wet a towel and cover its snout without covering the nose completely
despues: Refill your pet's water on the same day: it's the first thing they drink and the one most often forgotten
Check paws and pads (glass, staples, burns) when you get home
Wait a few days before bathing them: their own scent gives them a sense of security in a new place
Write down what was missing (food they didn't like, uncomfortable bowl) and fix it before next time

errores: Believing your pet will eat when hungry. A frightened dog or cat will leave the dry food. Offer wet food and sit with them; don't leave them alone with a bowl.
Taking them without a carrier "because they're very good". A frightened cat or dog will bite and run off; in an evacuation, a loose animal is a lost animal.
Forgetting your pet's water in the count. The family calculates 3 litres per person and forgets that the dog is another consumer.
Not bringing the vaccination record: without vaccines they won't be accepted at shelters or boarding facilities, and they may not be able to pass certain checks.
Leaving them at home with water and food "for two days". With no ventilation, no shops open and a damaged building, two days can be the last before they drop off the list of things that are fine.

secciones.intro: What your pet drinks and eats for three days. With no shops open and no fridge.

items.producto: Water for your pet (8 L bottle kept separate)
items.descripcion: A medium dog drinks about 1 litre a day and a cat about 250 ml. The bottle is separate from yours: don't compete for water.

items.producto: Extra pet food (dry food or cans for 72 h)
items.descripcion: A sealed reserve, kept visible, not a half-open sack. Dry food or cans, whatever they already eat: an emergency is no time to change their diet.

items.producto: Collapsible travel food and water bowls
items.descripcion: They take up no space and stop them drinking from a dirty makeshift bowl. With these you can give them water at a car stop.

items.producto: Wet food in cans (provides water and they'll eat it when stressed)
items.descripcion: A frightened animal refuses dry food but will usually accept canned food. The moisture helps them hydrate without drinking.

secciones.intro: If you have to leave in a hurry, this is what decides whether they come with you.

items.descripcion: With a door that closes properly. A loose cat in an evacuation is not coming back: it hides under the first car.
With the leash on and a spare one. In a panic, a dog breaks its usual leash and runs off toward the road.

items.producto: Muzzle (if required or if it is nervous around strangers)
items.descripcion: Required for PPP breeds and necessary if it is going to be surrounded by frightened people. A muzzled dog can board any transport.

items.producto: Blanket or towel with its home smell
items.descripcion: A new place is a threat to an animal; its blanket is the only sign that it is safe. It also provides warmth.
Lightweight alternative to a rigid carrier for rabbits, guinea pigs or small puppies.

secciones.intro: What lets you pass through a checkpoint, shelter or border with your pet.

items.producto: Vaccination card and a copy of the microchip in a waterproof folder
items.descripcion: Up-to-date vaccinations and microchip number: this is the document that proves the animal is yours. On paper, because the phone can run out of battery.
Insulin, heart medication, anti-epileptics, antiparasitic. If the animal takes something daily, the backpack carries a month's supply, not a week's.

items.producto: Basic veterinary first-aid kit (gauze, saline, povidone-iodine, bandages)
items.descripcion: Cuts on paws, burns or irritation of the eyes and ears. Saline solution cleans wounds and eyes without damaging them.

items.producto: Digital thermometer (shared with the general first-aid kit)
items.descripcion: It works for the animal and for people. Fever or hypothermia are measured the same way.

secciones.intro: Living with it for three days in an enclosed space without it being too noticeable.

items.descripcion: The same as you use at home, but with a spare supply: you will not be able to go out to the street for bags.

items.producto: Litter tray and cat litter (or puppy pads)
items.descripcion: A stressed cat without a litter tray retains urine and ends up at the vet. The disposable tray is good for two days.
For transport or the shelter: they protect the car trunk and surfaces if it cannot hold it in.
Paws, stuck-on sand and dirty fur without needing water. They work for the animal and for you.

secciones.intro: If it gets loose or if you have to go to different places, this is what allows it to return.

items.producto: ID tag with your phone number engraved
items.descripcion: A microchip has to be read with a scanner; an ID tag can be read by anyone. In an emergency with overwhelmed staff, the tag is faster.

items.producto: Recent photo of the pet with you (printed and on your phone)
items.descripcion: It is the most effective proof of ownership when there are no documents and the person who finds it doesn't know you.
A pet that doesn't sleep and won't stay still is a problem in a shelter. Its toy calms it more than any command.

secciones.titulo: Plan B: who cares for it if you can't
secciones.intro: The part almost nobody writes down and the one that is actually used most.

items.producto: Agreement with a trusted person (with keys and the pet's details)
items.descripcion: I'm hospitalized, away, or can't make it: someone with keys who knows where the food and carrier are and who knows the plan.

items.producto: List of boarding facilities and hotels that accept pets
items.descripcion: In an evacuation, not all shelters accept pets. Write down three places that accept them, with phone numbers, in your municipality and in the neighboring province.

items.producto: Pet data protection (digital copy of vaccination records with the microchip visible)
items.descripcion: Photos taken with your phone of the vaccination card, saved on an encrypted USB stick and in the cloud: if they ask for it remotely, you have it.

kit-frio.titulo: Cold/Winter Kit: 27 items to survive the cold (2026)
kit-frio.resumen: Cold kit: 27 items to survive extreme winter. Alternative heating, warm clothing and cold management 2026.
kit-frio.coste_total: 80-180 € (half if you use the winter clothing you already have)
kit-frio.paraQuien: For households with gas or electric heating (it goes down in a blackout), for people living in areas with snow or frost, and for older people and babies, who lose body heat before anyone else. Filomena left half of Spain without heating and unable to leave home.
kit-frio.paraQuien_no: It is not a mountaineering or extreme mountain snow kit: that requires technical equipment and training. Nor does it replace the basic rule: if you can't keep the house above 15 degrees, the plan is to go somewhere warm.

antes: Check that you have a carbon monoxide detector before using any combustion appliance indoors (heaters, burners, generators): CO has no smell and cannot be seen, and it kills in closed rooms
Prepare a 'refuge room': the smallest one with the fewest windows, to heat it and have everyone live there instead of trying to heat the whole house
Store the draft excluders/plastic to seal windows before it freezes: sticking them on at -4 degrees won't hold
Put the winter kit in the car before the snowfall, not during (check that the snow chains are your size and the tires aren't low)
Check on elderly neighbors: cold in the home isn't noticed, it builds up
durante: Never use a combustion stove or burner in a room without ventilation: leave a gap open and turn the appliance off before sleeping
Dress in layers (thermal, mid layer, windproof) and cover your head, hands and feet: that's where more than half your heat is lost
Drink water even if you're not thirsty: in cold weather you drink less and dehydration makes hypothermia worse
Don't go out to clear snow on an empty stomach or with wet shoes; and don't take the car without a scraper and full visibility
If you have to sleep at low temperatures, do it two together and with your clothes on: share the sleeping bag or blanket
despues: Check and clean the CO detector and restock batteries and fuel the same day: the second wave usually arrives within a week
Suspect frozen pipes: open the taps slowly before lighting the boiler; a pressure surge bursts the system
Restock salt, fuel and spent batteries: in snow, what runs out runs out across the whole area at once
Check the car's condition (battery, coolant, tires) as soon as you can get out

errores: Using the stove or burner in a closed room. It is the leading cause of CO poisoning during blackouts and snowstorms: the appliance consumes oxygen and gives off carbon monoxide.
Trying to heat the whole house. Without heating you don't heat a house, you heat a room: choosing a small one and closing off the rest is the difference between 12 and 18 degrees.

Dressing the baby or elderly person 'with one more layer' of cotton. Over cotton you need a layer that cuts wind and dries; and older people need to be taken out of the house when their hands turn cold and pale.
Storing the power bank and mobile phone in the car. Cold drains their battery: at 0 degrees they lose up to half their charge and don't recover well.
Going out into the snow without a reflective item or an ice scraper. Most deaths during snowfall are not from cold, they are from traffic accidents and pedestrians being hit.

secciones.titulo: Body heat: the layer that saves lives
secciones.intro: Without heating, your clothes are your home. And not just any clothes will do: wet cotton makes you cold.

items.producto: Thermal base layer (top and leggings, 2 sets)
items.descripcion: The layer closest to your skin matters most: thermal fabric wicks and dries, cotton stays wet and steals heat.
Second layer: traps the body's warm air. Wool keeps you warm even when slightly damp.
Cold feet are the first warning sign of hypothermia. Wool handles sweat much better than cotton.
A huge amount of heat is lost through the head. Day and night, indoors too.

items.producto: Warm gloves (and thin ones for tasks)
items.descripcion: Without hands you can't do anything: not cook, not open a frozen tap, not use your phone. Two pairs, one thin pair inside.

items.producto: Sleeping bag or warm one-piece pyjamas (current size + one spare)
items.descripcion: You can't sleep at 10 degrees in light pyjamas. A one-piece garment stops air getting in when you move.
It reflects body heat. It does not provide warmth on its own: you have to wrap yourself in it, not lay it over you like a sheet.

secciones.titulo: Safety: the silent enemy is CO
secciones.intro: When the heating fails, people improvise with combustion indoors. That is where tragedies happen.

items.producto: Battery-powered carbon monoxide (CO) detector with alarm
items.descripcion: Effectively mandatory if you are going to use any combustion appliance. CO has no smell, cannot be seen and does not wake you: it kills in your sleep.

items.producto: 1-2 kg ABC powder fire extinguisher with bracket
items.descripcion: Heaters and cables overheated by demand are the typical fire sources in a winter blackout.
If you run a generator or an extension lead to an electric heater, this device is the difference between a blown fuse and a fire.

secciones.intro: Heat one room, not the whole house. And always with ventilation and a detector.

items.producto: Butane gas heater with oxygen depletion cut-off
items.descripcion: The most effective option for a small room. It requires a cylinder, ventilation and a CO detector. Never use it for sleeping.

items.producto: Gas camping stove with canisters (for hot water and food)
items.descripcion: Hot water and hot food raise body temperature faster than any heater. Use outdoors or with a window open.
A hot drink every two hours is the cheapest way to keep your body at temperature. A thermos keeps it hot for 6 hours.
Lighting the heater or the camping stove with cold hands and gloves on is difficult. Long matches prevent burns.

secciones.titulo: Keep the cold out: the home
secciones.intro: Close the house up tight so you can heat just one room.

items.producto: Tape and plastic sheeting to seal windows and gaps
items.descripcion: An old, badly sealed window lets as much heat escape as a small heater can produce. Ten euros of plastic is worth more than turning the heater up.

items.producto: Thermal curtains or a wool blanket to cover the window
items.descripcion: At night, covering the glass is the cheapest improvement: glass is the coldest surface in the house.
A cold, damp house feels 3-4 degrees colder and ruins clothes. Humidity is half the problem of a winter without heating.

secciones.titulo: Outdoors and in the car: snow
secciones.intro: Filomena didn't leave people without heating: it left them unable to leave the house or take the car.

items.producto: Ice scraper and brush for the car
items.descripcion: Driving with a clean rectangle on the windshield is the cause of thousands of accidents every snowfall. And you have to clear the roof: the sheet falls off when you brake.

items.producto: Snow chains or textile snow socks
items.descripcion: On a highway in snow, you must drive in the right-hand lane and the left lanes are left free for snowplows (art. 32 RGC). Without chains you won't get up a mountain pass.

items.producto: Snow shovel and de-icing salt (or sand)
items.descripcion: To get out of the parking space and for the sidewalk. Salt also prevents a sheet of ice at your front door.

items.producto: Jumper cables and antifreeze with protection down to -25
items.descripcion: Cold kills the battery and freezes the coolant circuit. They are the two number-one failures during a cold snap.
In fog or snow, getting out to put down triangles is dangerous: the beacon is placed from inside the car and is now the only legal method since 1/1/2026.

items.producto: Light or reflective item for walking at night
items.descripcion: Mandatory for pedestrians on the shoulder of an interurban road at night or in poor visibility (art. 123 RGC). With snow, something reflective visible at 150 m is the only thing between you and a car.

secciones.intro: In winter it gets dark at 18:00, and a blackout leaves the house dark and without heating.

items.descripcion: With gloves on and in the dark you need both hands. A headlamp is the only useful light for moving around a cold house.
Snow warnings and closed roads come over the radio when the mobile network is overloaded or the antennas have no power.
Careful: cold cuts capacity by up to half if you keep it in the car. Keep it indoors, in an inside pocket if you go out.
Radio, flashlight and CO detector run on batteries. A CO detector with no batteries is just an ornament.

kit-terremoto.titulo: Earthquake Kit: 26 items for seismic protection (2026)
kit-terremoto.resumen: Earthquake kit: 26 items to protect you from falling objects and glass, shut off gas and water and call for help. Light, first-aid kit and cash: from 90 €.
kit-terremoto.coste_total: 90-170 € (much of it overlaps with the basic 72 h kit)
kit-terremoto.paraQuien: For anyone living in a seismic zone (south-east mainland Spain: Murcia, Almería, Granada, Málaga, Alicante) and, in fact, for any home: most earthquake damage doesn't come from the quake itself, it comes from falling objects and from gas and power cuts. It's the same kit that serves you in a blackout.
kit-terremoto.paraQuien_no: It's not a rescue or rubble kit: it won't turn you into a firefighter. Nor does it replace structural reinforcement, or knowing whether your building is one of those that holds up: that isn't solved with a backpack.

antes: Anchor shelves, the TV and tall wardrobes to the wall: the No. 1 cause of minor injuries in an earthquake is things falling off the walls
Find the gas and water shut-off valve and check that it turns: after the quake you'll have 30 seconds and shaking hands
Keep closed shoes and a flashlight next to the bed (under the bed, tied together): at night, the things that cut most are shards of glass on the floor
Agree on a meeting point outside the building and a contact outside the province: local lines get overloaded, outside ones don't
Keep the backpack near the exit door, not in the basement storage room
durante: Drop, take cover under a sturdy table and hold on to it: the table moves with you and protects you from falling objects
Don't run for the stairs or use the elevator: most injuries happen while fleeing and in stairwells
Stay away from windows, mirrors, shelves and building facades. If you are outside, go to an open space away from overhanging ledges and cables
If you are in a car, stop in an open area, not under a bridge, streetlights or power lines
If you smell gas, don't turn anything on: no lights, no matches, and no mobile phone near a leak
despues: Put on closed-toe shoes before walking around the house: broken glass is the leading cause of injuries and you can't see it in the dark
Shut off gas and water if there is a smell or damage, and don't turn on switches if you suspect a leak
Wait and listen to the radio: aftershocks are the norm in the following hours and instructions come via radio stations and ES-Alert
Don't go into damaged buildings or use the elevator; check the structure before staying (new cracks, doors that won't close)
Record damage with photos and report it to your insurance company and town council: aid is allocated by declared areas, and that requires documentation

errores: Running to the stairs as soon as the shaking starts. Most injuries happen while fleeing: in a stairwell, with people and falling objects. The right place is under a sturdy table.
Sleeping without shoes nearby and without a flashlight at hand. A nighttime earthquake + glass-covered floor = cut feet and darkness, just when you need to get out and help.
Lighting a match, turning on the light or using your mobile when you smell gas. It's the spark that causes the explosion. First shut off the gas, then everything else.
Not knowing where the gas valve is or not having a tool to shut it off. It's the first thing to do and almost no one has ever touched it.

Confusing “the house is still standing” with “the house is safe”. You need to check for new cracks, doors that won't close and damp before sleeping inside: aftershocks bring down what the first tremor left weakened.

secciones.titulo: Head and feet: the first things to break
secciones.intro: In an earthquake, what hurts you isn't the ground, it's what falls. And that day you discover you're barefoot.

items.descripcion: Cornices, lamps, shelves and partition bricks fall. A hard hat or bike helmet works and fits in the backpack.
For clearing debris, glass and overturned furniture. Without gloves you can't help anyone or clear your own exit.

items.producto: Sturdy closed-toe shoes next to the bed
items.descripcion: A pair of boots or sturdy shoes tied under the bed. Walking barefoot on broken glass is the most avoidable injury in a nighttime earthquake.

items.producto: Protective goggles (or sunglasses if you have nothing else)
items.descripcion: Dust, plaster and flying shards hit your eyes. Sunglasses cover them and serve as basic protection.

secciones.titulo: Water and food that need no cooking
secciones.intro: Gas may be cut off, there may be no power, and the water supply may come in cloudy. The rule is: cook nothing that needs more than opening a container.

items.producto: Bottled water (3 L per person per day)
items.descripcion: Six 1.5 L bottles per person for 72 hours. The water network is one of the first things to break and one of the last to be repaired.
If the water supply comes in cloudy or you have to use stored water, wait 30 minutes and it is drinkable. It weighs nothing and lasts for weeks.

items.producto: Ready-to-eat food that needs no cooking (canned goods, bars, nuts)
items.descripcion: Canned goods, nuts and bars: no gas or camping stove needed. Cold, ready food is Plan A after an earthquake.
Without power, an electric can opener is useless, and many cans have no ring pull. Five euros that can leave you without dinner.

items.producto: Dehydrated or ration food (in case it lasts longer)
items.descripcion: Supplies that last beyond 72 hours: an earthquake with structural damage can leave weeks of discomfort.

secciones.intro: If you are trapped or in the dark, this section is literally your voice.

items.descripcion: With debris and in the dark you need both hands. A headlamp goes on your head and lets you dig, help and walk.
A whistle can be heard farther than your voice and doesn't run out. Shouting for hours leaves you out of breath; a whistle doesn't. It is the cheapest rescue there is.
After an earthquake, radio broadcasts where the mobile network doesn't reach. It is your only source of instructions if the repeaters go down.
Your phone is your backup flashlight, your map and your way to call for help. Without battery, none of that exists.
Radio, flashlight and gas detector are battery-powered. Double spare set: in an emergency there’s no shop.
If you end up waiting for rescue in the open or in a car, it’s the only thing that prevents hypothermia. It takes up less space than a phone.

secciones.titulo: First-aid kit, medication and wound care
secciones.intro: An earthquake causes cuts and bruises, not rare accidents. And there are people with chronic conditions who can’t miss a dose.

items.producto: Complete first-aid kit (gauze, bandages, antiseptic, scissors)
items.descripcion: Cuts and bruises. You need to be able to clean and bandage without going to the emergency department, which will be overwhelmed.

items.producto: Chronic medication (7-30 days) with a copy of prescriptions
items.descripcion: People with diabetes, people on anticoagulants, people with high blood pressure, people with asthma. If your medication is in a closed pharmacy, you have a serious problem within 24 hours.

items.producto: Pocket first-aid kit to carry with you
items.descripcion: A small one with gauze and adhesive bandages for your pocket or bag: minor wounds can be treated right there.
With heat, dust, exertion and little water, it’s easy to get dehydrated. It’s also useful for diarrhea.

secciones.titulo: Shut off gas, water and electricity
secciones.intro: Earthquake damage is multiplied by what is left open afterwards. This is the first thing to do and nobody has it to hand.

items.producto: Shut-off key for gas and water (square-socket or universal key)
items.descripcion: Without it you can’t shut off the gas supply. After an earthquake, an open leak turns a scare into an explosion.
Pliers, screwdriver and blade in a pocket: cutting a stuck shutter or closing a valve without a tool.
To secure a door, lower something, make an improvised stretcher or hold down a tarp. 30 meters of rope handle the unpredictable.

secciones.intro: What you need for the hours that follow: breathing without dust, proving who you are and being able to pay without a card terminal.

items.descripcion: Dust from rubble and plaster irritates and damages the lungs. After an earthquake there is dust suspended in the air for days.

items.producto: Watertight folder or pouch with copies of documents
items.descripcion: ID card, deeds, policies, prescriptions: if the house is sealed off or damaged, papers are the difference between being able to claim and not being able to prove anything.
With no power or network, the card terminal doesn’t work and ATMs are down. 100-150 € in 10 and 20 € banknotes cover water, food and fuel.

items.producto: Digital copy on an encrypted USB drive
items.descripcion: Photos of the house and belongings before the earthquake: this is the proof the insurer asks for to assess damage.

kit-incendio.titulo: Fire Kit: 21 items for fire protection (2026)
kit-incendio.resumen: Wildfire kit: 21 items for a wildfire — breathe without smoke, get out in 10 minutes, defend the house and evacuate those who can't run. From 60 €.
kit-incendio.coste_total: 60-140 € (you already have most of it, or it also works for other emergencies)
kit-incendio.paraQuien: For people who live in the wildland-urban interface (homes next to woodland, residential developments, villages) or in areas of dry scrubland, an ever-growing part of Spain. And for anyone caught by smoke on the road.
kit-incendio.paraQuien_no: It is not a kit for staying behind to defend the house. If the authorities order an evacuation, a kit does not turn you into a firefighter or give you the right to stay: you evacuate.

antes: Clear 10 metres around the house: scrub, firewood, dry grass and hedges against the façade are the fuel that carries fire to your windows
Have metal sheets or wooden shutters to cover windows, and keep the backpack by the entrance, not at the back of the garage
Note down the municipal evacuation plan and the alternative route: in a fire, the road going up into the hills is the first to be closed
Mentally walk the exit at night: if a warning wakes you at 3:00 with smoke, you won't be able to improvise
Keep work clothes and closed-toe footwear within reach: synthetic clothing melts onto the skin
durante: Evacuate as soon as there is an order or smoke in the air, carrying only what is essential: a car is faster than a defended house
Close windows, doors and blinds to reduce drafts, and turn off ventilation and heating before leaving
If you are caught in the car: do not get out; wait with the windows closed, lights on and air on recirculation; the car offers more protection than running

If you are caught on foot: always move downhill and downwind (fire climbs the slope faster than you can), look for a clear area with no vegetation and, as a last resort, lie down in a place that has already burned
Cover your nose and mouth with a damp cloth and do not breathe through your mouth; smoke is more dangerous than the first line of flames
despues: Do not return until the authorities allow it: burned ground still has hot spots and roots are burning underground
When you arrive, do not turn anything on until you have checked the installations: the service line and meter are often damaged
Wet the outside and check the perimeter for hours: embers reignite with the wind
Report it if you suspect the origin and keep photos of the damage for the insurance and the local council

errores: Staying to defend the house when the fire is already close. Houses are defended beforehand (by clearing vegetation and wetting), not when the front is 200 meters away: from that point on, you only evacuate.
Taking the car towards the hills «because it is closer». The fire climbs the slope and cuts off the upper road first. The emergency exit is almost always downhill and downwind.
Wearing synthetic clothing and sandals. That is the combination that turns a touch of heat into a burn fused to the skin and makes evacuation on foot impossible.
Shouting to warn someone far away. Smoke leaves you without air within minutes: use a whistle and call, never run or shout.
Believing the danger ends when the fire front is out. Embers reignite with the wind, and burned trees and ground remain dangerous for hours afterwards.

secciones.titulo: Breathing: smoke kills before the fire
secciones.intro: In a wildfire, almost all victims die from inhalation. This section matters most.

items.descripcion: They filter smoke particles: fine ash, soot and thick smoke. A few minutes of smoke without protection and you genuinely become disoriented.
Smoke and sparks make your eyes water until you cannot see the exit. Closed goggles let you keep walking.

items.producto: Cotton cloths or towels (to wet and cover your mouth and nose)
items.descripcion: A damp cloth filters part of the smoke and cools the air. It is what people use when there is no mask, and it helps even if you have one.

items.producto: Water for drinking and for wetting cloths (8-10 L jerrycan or drum)
items.descripcion: Smoke dries out your throat, and with heat and stress you drink less than you should. It also wets cloths instantly.

secciones.intro: An evacuation order does not give you an afternoon to get ready. Whatever is not in this backpack stays behind.

items.descripcion: Already packed and by the door. If you have to fill it on the day, you’re losing the minutes that count.

items.producto: Waterproof folder with documents and some cash
items.descripcion: ID card, deeds, insurance policies, health card and cash in small banknotes. Rebuilding everything without paperwork is a year of bureaucracy.
Smoke reduces visibility to just a few metres and night can fall. With your hands free to carry, open and help.
Evacuation routes change with the wind. The radio gives the current instruction when mobile coverage fails.

items.producto: Physical map of your area (roads, alternative exits)
items.descripcion: If the network is overloaded or there’s no data, the paper map gets you out; GPS leaves you at the closed road like everyone else.
If you lose visibility in smoke, a whistle is what lets them find you. It fits in your pocket.

secciones.titulo: Clothing that won’t burn and stick to your skin
secciones.intro: What you’re wearing decides whether the heat just brushes you or burns you.

items.producto: Long-sleeved cotton or wool clothing (not synthetic)
items.descripcion: Polyester and nylon melt and stick to the skin. Cotton and wool protect and can get wet.

items.producto: Sturdy closed-toe footwear (boot or tough shoe)
items.descripcion: No sandals: burnt ground and embers go through thin soles. And you can’t run in flip-flops.
For opening a hot metal door, grabbing a hose or moving something hot. Without gloves you can’t touch anything.

items.producto: Cotton cap or scarf to cover your head and neck
items.descripcion: Radiant heat and embers fall from above. Covering your head prevents burns to your hair and neck.

secciones.titulo: Defend the house if there’s still time
secciones.intro: Only while there is no evacuation order. Ten minutes of preparation can save the house; one minute too many can cost you your life.

items.producto: Long reinforced hose (plus a sprinkler or nozzle)
items.descripcion: To wet the perimeter, the facade and nearby scrub areas. The most effective thing before the fire front arrives.

items.producto: 6 kg ABC dry powder extinguisher (or several 2 kg ones)
items.descripcion: For fires that reach the house: roof, stacked firewood or a vehicle. A car extinguisher is not enough.

items.producto: Hoe, rake and manual brush cutter
items.descripcion: Removing dry grass and leaf litter around the perimeter is what prevents a ground fire from reaching the façade.
It is used to put out incipient fires and soak hotspots without a hose or power. Very useful when the power goes out and the pump does not work.

secciones.titulo: Animals and people who cannot run on their own
secciones.intro: An evacuation is measured by the slowest person, not the fastest.

items.producto: Pet carrier and leash to hand (pets)
items.descripcion: In a smoke evacuation, a loose animal hides or runs off into the wild. With a carrier, it leaves with you on the first trip.

items.producto: Chronic medication and list of treatments (older people or dependent people)
items.descripcion: Anticoagulants, insulin, inhalers, psychiatric treatments. They go in the backpack with a copy of prescriptions, not in the bathroom cabinet.

items.producto: Spare cane, walker or folding chair
items.descripcion: Whoever walks slowly sets the pace; having a backup mobility aid prevents the evacuation from getting stuck.

kit-comunicacion.titulo: Communication Kit: walkie-talkies, radio and satellite messenger (2026)
kit-comunicacion.resumen: Off-grid communication kit: licence-free PMR446 walkie-talkies, hand-crank radio and satellite messenger. 6 items from 80 € so you don't miss alerts.
kit-comunicacion.coste_total: 80-300 € (PMR446 walkie-talkies + battery radio and power bank; more with satellite messenger)
kit-comunicacion.paraQuien: For any household that wants to be able to alert and be alerted when all networks go down at once: long blackout, DANA, fire or lockdown.
kit-comunicacion.paraQuien_no: It does not replace your mobile phone for everyday use, nor does it let you make long-distance calls without an amateur radio licence. And it is not a toy: if you don't test it beforehand, you won't know how to use it on the day of the emergency.

antes: Agree on a fixed family channel and subcode (channel 7, subcode 7) and write it on each walkie-talkie
Test the real range: one at home and one out on the street; in the city it reaches much less than the box promises
Tune in and save the useful stations (regional and Radio Nacional) before putting the radio away
Keep spare batteries outside the devices and a short cable with the power bank
If you have a satellite messenger, set up emergency contacts and test sending a message
durante: Listen before transmitting: two stations at once block the channel with a squeal
Keep messages short and speak slowly; repeat numbers and addresses twice
Radio on at least twice a day to listen to official alerts
Don't saturate the mobile network with calls: SMS messages get through when calls don't
Agree on a fixed contact time so you don't use up battery all day
despues: Recharge walkie-talkies, power bank and messenger, and replace dead batteries
Write down what failed (range, channel with interference) and fix it
Check your satellite subscription if you have one: don't let it lapse

errores: Not testing the walkie-talkies beforehand: an unused device is an expensive brick.
Buying walkie-talkies that aren't PMR446: many cheap devices use bands that do require a license.
Relying on the satellite messenger for everything: if it runs out of battery, you're left unable to communicate.
Storing batteries inside the radio: they corrode and ruin the device.
Calling instead of texting: in an emergency, voice calls collapse before short messages.

secciones.intro: No license, no coverage and no internet. PMR446 has been legal in Spain since 1998 and lets you talk radio to radio when there is no network.

items.descripcion: Pair of rechargeable PMR446 walkie-talkies with charging base: 16 channels and 0.5 W, legal in Spain without a license or paperwork.
Better antenna and sensitivity: up to 5-10 km in open field.

secciones.titulo: Listen and alert the outside world
secciones.intro: When the mobile network goes down, the radio still broadcasts official alerts and the satellite message still gets through.

items.producto: Battery or dynamo FM/AM radio (with flashlight)
items.descripcion: The only source of information if internet and phone networks go down. With a dynamo, no batteries required.
The rechargeable walkie-talkie and the phone die at the same time. Two outputs keep them alive for several days.
Messages and SOS via satellite network where there is no mobile coverage. Requires a clear sky and an active monthly subscription.
If stored inside the radio, they corrode: keep them separate, in their packaging. Mixed pack for radio, flashlight and remote control.

kit-starlink.titulo: Starlink Kit: satellite internet for emergencies (2026)
kit-starlink.resumen: Starlink Kit: satellite internet with a clear sky from any location (400-600 € + 50-60 €/mes), backup 4G router and satellite messenger as a last resort.
kit-starlink.paraQuien: For anyone living in areas without mobile coverage or fibre, for anyone who wants real communications redundancy in an emergency, or for anyone working in rural areas where the fixed network fails. Starlink works from any point with a clear view of the sky.
kit-starlink.paraQuien_no: It is not for anyone with mobile coverage and fibre that never fail: there you can wait. It also requires ~100° of clear sky (trees and mountains block the signal) and a monthly subscription: without it, the hardware is a brick.
kit-starlink.busc: starlink portable terminal gen 3 4g emergency router

antes: Check Starlink coverage in your area: the official app shows sky visibility and installation forecasts.
Check the coverage of two different operators at your location: redundancy only exists if both have signal.
Calculate the total budget: terminal (500-1,200 €) + subscription (45-60 €/month) + router (300-800 €) + inReach (~400 €).
Plan the location: a roof with 100° of clear sky or an outdoor mast of 2+ metres. Avoid balconies with obstructions.
durante: Activate Starlink and its subscription. Use the app to find the optimal installation point by scanning the sky.
Test the speed. Readjust if there is high latency (>100 ms) or packet loss.
Configure the 4G/5G router with dual SIM and automatic failover between the two operators.
Activate the inReach and its plan; test sending a message and geolocation.
despues: Clean the Starlink panel every 2-3 months: dust, fallen leaves and droppings reduce the signal.
Renew subscriptions before they expire: when reactivating, the price sometimes changes.
Test the inReach every month: test message and geolocation. A dead battery does not save lives.
Check antennas and connections every 6 months: wind, rain and salt air damage the contacts.

errores: Installing Starlink with an obstructed view. It needs ~100° of clear sky; trees, roofs or mountains block the signal. A roof or terrace with an open view, not the balcony.
Forgetting the monthly subscription. Without it, the terminal is a 500-1,200 € brick. Residential plan (50-60 €/month) or mobile (45 €/month).
No redundancy (Starlink + 4G/5G router). A single means of communication is a single point of failure: with extreme weather and no cellular coverage, you would be left without communications.

secciones.intro: Satellite internet when everything goes down: mobile phones, fiber, LTE. Real 50-200 Mbps without terrestrial infrastructure, always with a clear view of the sky: trees, roofs and mountains block the signal.

items.descripcion: Satellite internet where there is no coverage or fiber, with the antenna pointed at a clear sky. Real 50-200 Mbps. Antenna and Wi-Fi router included. The subscription is essential: without it, the hardware is useless.

items.producto: Mounting bracket for Starlink (roof / wall / mast)
items.descripcion: Fixes the antenna to a roof, wall or mast and gives you the extra sky view that balcony installation does not. Compatible with Starlink Standard (Gen 3), V3, 4 and 4X.

items.producto: Ethernet extension cable for Starlink (30 m)
items.descripcion: Extends the antenna cable to the point with a clear sky. Waterproof, for outdoor use. Compatible with Starlink Standard 4/4X/Gen 3/V4/V5.

secciones.intro: Cellular connectivity as a backup to Starlink: useful when satellite is not viable (dense forests, extreme weather) or as a second option.

items.descripcion: 12-16 dBi: boosts the signal when coverage is weak. Roof-mounted with cable to the router.

secciones.intro: With no mobile coverage, the satellite messenger is the last network — but it also needs a clear sky: under a roof or in a ravine, the SOS will not go out. It is the backup for the phone, not for the sky.

items.descripcion: SOS, geolocation and two-way satellite messaging, up to 350 h of battery life. Requires a clear sky and an active subscription: under a roof, in a ravine or with dense forest, the SOS will not transmit.
Keeps the inReach and the phone charged when there is no mains power. USB-C charging.

kit-electricidad.titulo: Electricity Kit: 10 items to have light without the grid (2026)
kit-electricidad.resumen: Electricity kit: power for the essentials with a solar panel, SAI and cables — light, router and portable fridge without the grid. From 200 €.
kit-electricidad.coste_total: 100-250 € (power bank + lights + batteries) up to 500-900 € (with solar generator and LiFePO4 battery)
kit-electricidad.paraQuien: Any household that wants light and minimal communication when the power grid fails: apartments with a balcony (folding panel) or houses with a roof.
kit-electricidad.paraQuien_no: It does not replace a fuel generator for tools or air conditioning: that is another level of budget and windows.

antes: Calculate your real watts: add up the essentials (LED lights, router, mobile phone, fridge if you can) and buy above that
Place the solar panel where it gets direct sun for most of the day; in winter it produces half
Charge EVERYTHING to 100% every Sunday: a battery at 60% on the day of the blackout is a useless battery
Use LED lights with built-in batteries: they use 10 times less than any alternative
Keep cables together and labelled: in the dark there is no time to test which is which
durante: Power lights, mobile phone and radio first; the fridge only if your generator can handle the start-up surge
The router uses little: keeping the internet alive can be worth more than a fridge
Recharge during the day with the panel; use the battery at night: never both at once
Turn off and unplug what you do not use: devices on standby eat the battery without giving you anything
despues: Recharge everything to 100% again before storing the kit
Note how many hours it lasted and what you used: next time you will buy better
Check battery cycles: if capacity drops below 80%, it is time to replace it

errores: Buying a generator without calculating watts: 300 W will not start a fridge (it needs a 1,200 W surge).
Leaving the power bank half charged: it self-discharges and on the day of the blackout it is dead.
Confusing Wh with mAh: 20,000 mAh is only 74 Wh, not 20 hours of fridge.
Putting the solar panel in the shade or behind glass: it produces half or less.
Using candles unattended: it is the leading cause of fires in blackouts.

1,280 Wh actual, 3,000–6,000 cycles. The serious option for those preparing for outages lasting days.

kit-kit-profesional.paraQuien: For households that cannot afford to be without power, data or food: rural homes far from services, businesses that depend on servers, or anyone seeking real independence from outages and infrastructure crises.
kit-kit-profesional.paraQuien_no: It is not a kit for surviving months off-grid. High investment (2.000-5.000 €), it needs space (roof or land for panels, a ventilated area for batteries and generator) and professional installation, and it requires maintenance. It is not 'install and forget'.
kit-kit-profesional.busc: professional kit autonomy solar energy lithium battery starlink generator

antes: Calculate your daily consumption: kWh/month ÷ 30 = kWh/day. The kit should cover 70–80% of that consumption.
Identify where to install the panels: south-facing roof, flat roof or adjacent ground. Minimum 4 m² per 400W.
Prepare the battery space: ventilated area, 10-25 °C, away from flammable materials.
Locate the generator site: outdoors, on firm ground and more than 6 metres from windows, doors and vents (the CDC specifies 20 feet), with access for refuelling.
If you don't know how to install it: budget for an electrician + certified solar installer. It's not witchcraft, but it has to be done right.
durante: Batteries and inverter first, then panels, then Starlink. Test each module before connecting the next one.
Check polarities before connecting: negative to negative, positive to positive. A short circuit in batteries is immediate.
Set the inverter's low cut-off voltage (11.5V on 12V; 40V on 48V) so deep discharges don't damage the batteries.
Activate Starlink and its subscription. Test the speed; readjust the position if there's high latency or packet loss.
Test the generator outdoors: 30 minutes under load, stabilised fuel.
despues: Clean the panels every 2-3 months: dust, fallen leaves and droppings cut efficiency by 20-30%.
Check connections and fuses every 6 months: corrosion, loose screws and frayed cables cause most failures.
Battery test once a month: voltage and temperature. A cell that runs hotter than the others is going to fail.
Test the generator every 3 months (30 min under load). Don't leave petrol in the tank for more than 6 months.
Renew the Starlink plan before it expires: the price sometimes changes when you reactivate.

errores: Buying panels without an inverter or batteries. Panels only generate with sun: without storage you have nothing at night. Batteries and inverter first, then panels.
Installing lead-acid batteries in 2026. LFP lithium costs 3-4× more but lasts 5× longer (3,000+ cycles vs 500-1,000): it works out cheaper per cycle.
Putting Starlink up with an obstructed view. It needs ~100° of clear sky; trees, roofs or mountains cut the signal. Roof or terrace with an open view.

Putting the generator inside the home. CO is invisible and odourless and kills within minutes: always outdoors, more than 6 metres from windows, doors and vents, and never in the house or garage even with the doors open.
Do not DIY the installation. Poorly anchored panels fly off, incorrectly connected batteries catch fire, unprotected cables melt. 200-500 € for certified installation is worth every euro.

calentar-casa-sin-electricidad-invierno.titulo: How to heat your home without electricity in winter: 6 methods that work (2026)
calentar-casa-sin-electricidad-invierno.resumen: Without power, the temperature drops 2 °C per hour. A guide with 6 real methods: insulation, stoves, blankets and power stations. Data from AEMET and Protección Civil.
calentar-casa-sin-electricidad-invierno.cuerpo:
When the power goes out in the middle of winter, the first problem isn't the darkness or a dead phone battery: it's the cold coming into your home. A home without heating can lose between 2 and 4 °C per hour on a Spanish winter night. In 6 hours, it goes from 18 °C to 6 °C — a temperature that already poses a risk of hypothermia for children and older adults.

This winter (2026-2027), the State Meteorological Agency (AEMET) forecasts below-average temperatures across most of the peninsula, with episodes of intense cold and isolated snow. Protección Civil recommends being prepared: a winter blackout can become a risky situation within a few hours.

Before buying anything: 4 insulation techniques (0 €)

The cheapest and most effective method is to stop heat from escaping. If you have gas, electric, or pellet heating and it's working, these techniques multiply its efficiency. If you have nothing, they are your only line of defense:

1. Close off rooms you don't use

Less volume = less heat to maintain. Close doors and, if a room has drafts from the windows, temporarily seal it with rolled-up towels at the threshold. According to the IDAE (Institute for Energy Diversification and Saving), closing off an unheated room creates an air pocket that acts as extra insulation, reducing heat loss by 15-20%.

2. Insulate the windows

Windows account for up to 25% of heat loss in an average Spanish home (IDAE data). If you have blinds, close them at night — the air gap between the glass and the blind is a natural insulator. An extra trick: place cardboard or newspaper on the inside of the window fixed with temporary tape. It isn't pretty, but it raises the perceived temperature by 2-3 °C.

3. Cover the floor

The floor loses between 10% and 15% of the heat. Thick rugs, old blankets, or even cardboard boxes underfoot act as a thermal barrier. If you have carpet, clean it — dust reduces its insulating capacity by 10-15%.

4. The three-layer rule

Three thin shirts retain more heat than one thick one: the air trapped between layers is the real insulator. Thick socks are essential — cold feet cool the whole body through circulation. Gloves indoors aren't an exaggeration: you lose significant heat through your hands.

Method 1: Butane heater (the most practical)

The butane (propane) heater is the most widespread method in Spain for emergency heating. A 12 kg cylinder can last between 2 and 3 days with intermittent use at medium power, and the cost per hour is around 0,09-0,11 € (at 0,38 €/kg).

Strengths: immediate ignition, no electricity needed, low cost, widely available cylinders. Weaknesses: produces moisture, requires minimum ventilation and consumes oxygen.

Safety rule: always with a window slightly open (100 cm² of ventilation) and a CO detector. Protección Civil makes it clear: ventilation is not optional.

View portable butane heaters on Amazon →

Method 2: Catalytic heater (the most efficient)

Catalytic technology generates heat without a visible flame through a chemical reaction on a ceramic panel. The result: lower consumption (110-280 g/h compared with 280-305 g/h for traditional heaters), no open flame (safer with children and pets), and more even heat.

The catalytic panel is a consumable that lasts about two winters; replacing it costs around 30-40 €. With 4 hours of daily use, a 12 kg cylinder can last up to two weeks.

View catalytic heater Orbegozo H 55 on Amazon →

Method 3: Fireplace or pellet stove

If you already have a fireplace or pellet stove installed, it's the most natural way to heat several rooms. Modern pellet stoves have an efficiency above 85% (the National Institute of Industrial Technology measures efficiencies between 85-92%).

Limitation: most need electricity to power the hopper and fan. In a blackout, they only work if you have a SAI or a connected power station. Check the blackout kit to see which power stations support this type of stove.

View wood pellets for stoves on Amazon →

Method 4: Gas stove for heating (emergencies only)

In a pinch, the gas stove (butane or natural gas) can be used to heat a room. Warning: only for brief emergencies (maximum 1-2 hours) and ALWAYS with plenty of ventilation. It is not a heating method — it is an emergency resource.

A gas oven at 200 °C emits approximately 2,000 W of heat. Leaving the door ajar (never closed, risk of gas accumulation) can heat the kitchen by 2 to 4 °C.

The blackout kit includes everything you need to cook without power

Method 5: Thermal blankets and indoor tents

The emergency thermal blanket (the gold or silver ones for 2 €) reflects up to 90% of radiated body heat. It works best wrapped inside a normal blanket — the blanket protects from the wind and the thermal blanket reflects heat.

A small tent (for warmth) inside the home creates a microclimate that can raise the internal temperature by 5 to 8 °C. Mountaineers have been doing this for decades: a small space, isolated from the rest of the home, is warmed by body heat and blankets. See the mountain kit as a reference to understand survival logic.

View emergency thermal blankets on Amazon →

Method 6: Power station + electric radiator

A 1,000 Wh power station can power a small oil-filled radiator (1,000 W) for approximately 45-60 minutes. That's not much, but it's enough to keep a room at a reasonable temperature overnight if combined with the insulation techniques above.

The trick is not to use the power station for continuous heating: use it as occasional backup (2-3 hours) while you optimize insulation. The power station in the blackout kit is a supplement, not a replacement.

Thermal blanket0 €PerfectLow (body only)Essential supplement
Power station0,15-0,20 €PerfectMediumOccasional backup (2-3 h)

Warning signs: when to call 112

It's not a matter of comfort, it's a matter of safety. If the indoor temperature drops below 10 °C and there are vulnerable people (children under 6, adults over 65, people with respiratory or cardiovascular conditions), the situation should be treated as an emergency.

The symptoms of mild hypothermia are: uncontrollable shivering, difficulty speaking, clumsy movements. At temperatures below 5 °C, the risk increases exponentially. The 112 Especial app from Protección Civil lets you request help when the line is overloaded — have it downloaded before the crisis hits.

The lesson of the Spanish winter

Recent winters in Spain have shown that preparation costs less than suffering. A cheap butane heater (60-80 €), thermal blankets (2-5 €), and a CO detector (15-25 €) add up to less than 120 € — less than a month of conventional electric heating.

The most important thing isn't the equipment: it's deciding before the power goes out which room you'll stay in, how you'll insulate it, and what heat source you'll use. A decision made in panic, at 10 at night and in the cold, is almost always a bad decision.

The cold/winter kit has all of this organized by priority — heater, blankets, insulation, CO detector — so you don't have to decide when the cold is already inside your home.

Safety: what the regulations say about gas heaters

According to the Official State Gazette, butane/propane gas heaters are regulated by the Ministry for Ecological Transition (formerly MITECO). Every heater must include at least:

  • Flame failure cut-off system (thermocouple)
  • Atmosphere analyzer (cut-off if CO₂ exceeds safe levels)
  • Piezo ignition (without direct contact with the pilot flame)

The three heaters in this comparison comply with these standards. In addition, Civil Protection always recommends keeping a window slightly open (about 100 cm² of ventilation) and checking the official Civil Protection recommendations during cold spells.

Catalytic heater vs blue-flame heater: which is better?

The main difference is how the heat is produced. The catalytic heater generates heat without a visible flame through a chemical reaction on the ceramic panel. The blue-flame one shows a real (blue) flame that heats the surrounding ceramic panel.

Advantages of the catalytic heater: lower consumption (110-280 g/h compared with 280-305 g/h), no open flame (safer with children), more even heat and it dries out the air less.

Advantages of the blue-flame heater: higher power (up to 4200 W), faster heating, no catalytic panel replacement required, slightly lower price.

For most Spanish families, the Orbegozo H 55 offers the best balance of quality, price and consumption among catalytic heaters. For large rooms (living room >30 m²), 4200 W heaters (Cecotec ReadyWarm 4000, Orbegozo HCE 73) heat up faster.

mejor-cocina-portatil-gas-apagon.titulo: Best portable gas stove for power outages (2026): 5 models compared
mejor-cocina-portatil-gas-apagon.resumen: Gas camping stove: which is best for cooking without electricity during a power outage, how much it consumes and how much it costs to keep your family fed
mejor-cocina-portatil-gas-apagon.cuerpo:
Why a portable gas stove is essential when the power goes out

When electricity goes out, the first impulse is to open the fridge. But frozen food thaws in hours and canned foods need cooking to be safe. A portable gas stove is the only tool that heats water, cooks canned food and prepares hot food without depending on any outlet, battery or grid connection.

Protección Civil recommends that every household keep supplies for at least 72 hours, and in winter that self-sufficiency is not much use if you cannot heat water for tea, coffee, soup or pasta. A three-day blackout without the ability to cook becomes a hydration and malnutrition crisis within 48 hours.

Camping gas stoves used for hiking are also perfect for household emergencies. They are compact, inexpensive, run on butane or LPG canisters available at any gas station and supermarket, and heat as well as a conventional kitchen burner.

Quick comparison: the five selected models

All camping gas stoves have a key advantage in an emergency: efficiency. They consume between 40 and 60 g/h per 1,000 W of power, which translates into 4 to 6 hours of continuous cooking on a single 220 g canister. For a family of four that needs to prepare two hot meals a day during a three-day blackout, two 220 g canisters would be enough (or one 230 g canister if shared with the butane heater).

1. Coleman K2 Plus: the most versatile for emergency cooking

The Coleman K2 Plus is the most balanced model for household use during a blackout. Its flame-regulation system lets you go from a rapid boil to a slow simmer with the same control as a conventional gas stove. The folding grate attaches to the 220 g canister and can support pots up to 3 kg.

Most notable is its size: it fits in the 72h kit backpack (4.5 × 30 × 30 cm folded) and weighs only 500 g with the canister included. For a family that shares the K2 with the butane heater, a 220 g canister lasts approximately 5–6 hours of intermittent cooking — enough for two meals over a couple of days.

It includes a piezoelectric ignition system (no lighter or matches needed) and a built-in wind guard that improves efficiency by 30% outdoors. It works perfectly indoors, although it is recommended to ventilate the kitchen for at least two minutes every 30 minutes of use.

See Coleman K2 Plus on Amazon

2. Coleman CombiCook: two in one, ideal for families

The CombiCook combines a gas burner on the left with a heating plate (griddle type) on the right. Both run on the same butane canister, so you can cook two things at once: boil water for pasta and heat canned food on the plate at the same time.

This duality is key in a blackout where cooking time becomes a scarce resource. With the K2 Plus, a family of four has to cook in two batches; with the CombiCook, both meals are prepared in a single round. During a prolonged blackout, that time efficiency translates into lower gas consumption and greater responsiveness.

The weight (1.3 kg) makes it a little bulkier than the K2, but it still fits in a medium emergency backpack. Its price (~55 €) is 50% higher than the K2, but the extra functionality justifies the investment for families with small children who need different preparations at the same time.

See Coleman CombiCook on Amazon

3. Bonaverde Camping: the most economical option

The Bonaverde is a basic bayonet-cartridge stove (the type of cylindrical canister that screws on top) with 3,000 W of raw power. It has no precise flame regulator or wind guard, but it boils a liter of water in 2.5 minutes — the same as an electric kettle, but without a plug.

At ~22 €, it is the cheapest stove in this comparison, and for occasional emergency use it is more than enough. The weak point is its consumption: at maximum power it uses about 200 g of gas per hour, which means only about 3–4 hours of cooking with one cartridge. For a three-day blackout, you would need at least four spare cartridges.

It also lacks a stable base for heavy pots: it is recommended not to exceed 2 kg on the grate. If your family prepares heavy soups and stews, the Bonaverde falls short in a prolonged emergency.

See Bonaverde on Amazon

4. Esbit HSB-1: the ultralight tablet stove

The Esbit HSB-1 does not use gas: it burns solid fuel tablets (hexamethylenetetramine) sold in packs of 200 for ~15 €. Each tablet lasts 25–30 minutes and heats water for coffee, tea or instant soup.

Its advantage is the total absence of an open flame (it burns without a spark, at low temperature) and its ridiculous weight: 250 g without fuel, it fits in a pocket. It is ideal as a secondary stove to heat drinks, prepare dehydrated soups or water-purification tablets in a blackout scenario where hydration is the priority.

But it is not suitable for cooking canned food, boiling water in quantity or preparing dishes that require prolonged cooking. Its use is limited to "ready-to-eat" preparations or simple heating. For a complete food emergency, it should be paired with a more powerful gas stove.

5. Kampa Tarn 2.1: balance between power and safety

The Kampa Tarn 2.1 is a bayonet-cartridge stove with 2,200 W, a precise flame regulator and a stable three-leg base that makes it very safe on uneven surfaces (camping tables, kitchen counters with vibration). Its automatic shut-off system cuts the gas when the cartridge is disconnected, an extra safety feature in domestic settings.

At ~30 € and 450 g, it sits midway between the Bonaverde (cheaper but less safe) and the Coleman K2 (more expensive but more adjustable). It is the recommended option for those who prioritize stability and control over maximum power.

A 12 kg butane canister is not compatible with camping stoves — these only use small 220 g canisters or bayonet cartridges.

Safety rules for cooking without electricity

Portable gas stoves are safe when used correctly. These rules are non-negotiable:

  • Always in ventilated areas: even if the stove is inside the house (kitchen or dining room), open a window for at least two minutes every 30 minutes of use. Combustion consumes oxygen and produces CO₂.
  • Never use the stove in a closed space: without ventilation, carbon monoxide (CO) builds up without you noticing. A CO detector is mandatory (such as the one in the blackout kit).
  • Secure the surface: place the stove on a flat, stable base. Uneven surfaces (camping tables) require a heat-resistant metal or ceramic base.
  • Keep canisters away from heat: do not store spare canisters near the butane heater or other heat sources. Heat expands them and can cause leaks.
  • Never leave the stove unattended: even with piezoelectric ignition and automatic shut-off, the flame should never be left alone.
  • Keep the extinguisher nearby: a dry powder extinguisher (ABC type) less than two meters from the cooking area is the only fire protection if something goes wrong.

Gas vs electricity: which is more practical in a blackout?

Induction stoves are more efficient (90% of energy becomes heat, compared with 55% for gas), but they require electricity. A 1,000 Wh power station can run a 1,500 W induction burner for approximately 40 minutes before needing a recharge. A three-day blackout becomes a race against time.

Gas, by contrast, does not need recharging. A 220 g canister provides ~8–9 kWh of thermal energy (the calorific value of butane is ~10.3 kWh/kg). With two canisters, you have enough to cook three meals a day for three full days, without depending on any outlet or battery.

For a short blackout (one day), the power station may be enough. For any emergency that lasts longer, gas is the most practical and predictable option.

Final verdict

The best portable gas stove for a 2026 blackout is the Coleman K2 Plus: precise flame regulation, extreme portability (500 g), automatic ignition system and moderate consumption. At ~35 € it is accessible for any household and two 220 g canisters are enough to cover three days of hot meals.

If your priority is cooking for a family of four and you want to maximize efficiency, the Coleman CombiCook (simultaneous plate + burner) deserves the extra investment. For tighter budgets, the Bonaverde offers the same power for half the price.

And remember: a stove is useless without fuel. If you know that cold weather is frequent in winter, include two extra butane canisters in your cold/winter kit, along with the heater and thermal blankets.

kit-que-salva-la-musica-espanola.titulo: The kit C. Tangana would buy to save Spanish music (2026)
kit-que-salva-la-musica-espanola.resumen: A blackout like the one on 29-O doesn't distinguish between a hospital and a recording studio. We imagine, piece by piece and with real links, the equipment that
kit-que-salva-la-musica-espanola.cuerpo:
C. Tangana filled stadiums singing that «el madrileño» doesn’t give up. But there is one thing that neither he nor any artist can beat by sheer willpower: a blackout. On 29-O we saw it on a national scale — the power, coverage and access went out — and what began as an anecdote ended up being the best demonstration of why Spanish music literally depends on a plug.

Think about it: a tour is a truckload of amplifiers that need power in every venue. The studio is a tower of machines that can’t take a power outage in the middle of a take. And the entire business — streaming, merchandising, tickets — lives in the cloud, which turns out to be in a datacenter that does have generators, because someone remembered to buy them. This article is an editorial exercise: if “CT” called us tomorrow and said “don’t let the music stop”, this is what we’d put in the two bags — the ones from the brand photo, you know.

Minute 0: the power goes out in the middle of a mix

The first one hit isn’t the concert, it’s the studio. A 200-millisecond outage erases the session, fries a power supply and shuts off the router right when you were uploading the master. The first thing an energy professional buys isn’t a generator: it’s a SAI (the classic “UPS”), a bridge battery that gives 10–20 minutes to save, close and shut down without drama. It’s the cheapest and most cost-effective item on the whole list: a 600–900 VA SAI covers the router, ONT and the mixing computer for the price of a dinner.

And for what can’t tolerate even a 10-minute interruption — the laptop where Ableton lives — a 20,000 mAh power bank with AC output keeps the session alive all night. It’s not poetry: it’s the difference between losing a take and losing the afternoon.

Hour 2: tonight’s concert can’t be canceled

Here the world changes: 3,000 ticket holders aren’t going home because the power grid had a bad day. A small stage can be kept going with a 300–500 Wh portable solar generator: session sound, monitors, backline lighting and the crew’s phones. It won’t run a stadium PA system — that’s a different league — but it saves the acoustic set, the small room and the masterclass.

The formula used by those who know is combined: the battery stores, the 60–100 W folding solar panel recharges silently (the neighbors appreciate that it isn’t a gasoline generator at 2 in the morning), and if things drag on, a 100 Ah LiFePO4 battery multiplies the runtime tenfold. It’s the same architecture we recommend in any electricity kit, except here we load it with meaning: without energy there is no culture.

Hour 6: the city is dark and the team needs to be organized

A long blackout turns any tour crew into an emergency team. That’s where the devices nobody would associate with music come in, and they save the day:

  • Seeing in the dark without killing the battery: a hands-free LED headlamp for loading the van, and a rechargeable area light for the backline.
  • Knowing what’s happening: if data goes down, a battery-powered FM/AM radio is the only channel still broadcasting (and yes, SER would still be reporting the news with or without streaming).
  • Coordinating without coverage: a pair of PMR446 walkie-talkies between FOH and stage saves half an hour of shouting across an empty venue.
  • The beers (and the ham): a portable cooler isn’t a whim — in an emergency, preserving is part of the plan.

The comparison: three setups depending on the size of your “tour”

The same applies to anyone with a rehearsal room, a neighborhood studio or who simply doesn’t want their music (or their life) to depend on the main switch. Three budgets, same idea:

SetupWhat it includesEstimated cost
Balcony sessionSAI + AC power bank + headlamp120-250 €
Neighborhood studiothe above + 300–500 Wh solar generator + folding panel + surge-protected power strip400-700 €
Tour with no excusesthe above + 100 Ah LiFePO4 + walkies + area light + portable cooler800-1.400 €

The surge-protected power strip in the middle row is the accessory everyone forgets: when the power comes back, it comes back with a surge that destroys entire power supplies. It costs less than an instrument cable.

The lesson the blackout leaves behind

C. Tangana hasn’t asked for this (note: this is an editorial imagining, not a sponsorship — as Affiliates we only earn if you buy through the links, and the artist hasn’t seen this article). But the underlying idea is his almost without knowing it: doing things right, without depending on someone else to fix them for you. This country’s power grid holds up as well as it holds up; your studio, venue or next live show’s gear can hold up much longer if you decide before the next 29-O.

To put together the complete kit step by step, with a usage guide and common mistakes: Kit Apagón page, Kit Electricidad page and Kit Comunicación page. And if you want the more refined studio version, the satellite internet one so the cloud session never drops, it’s this one.
